These $90 Corduroys Are So Buttery You Could Baste a Turkey With Them

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It’s an unfortunate situation for a number of reasons, but each one of those is personal, and that’s what therapy is for.
  • Because they’re made from one of the most buttery, wide-ish wale corduroy fabrics I’ve seen a substantial brand use in ages, the first thing that you’ll notice about these is how soft they are, because, brother.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If there was one thing I could’ve told you about my winter wardrobe a month ago, it was that I was good on corduroys. In the past decade, I’ve acquired double-knee corduroys, patchwork corduroys, five-pocket corduroys, straight-leg corduroys, corduroys that are also painter’s pants, corduroy climbing pants and not one but two pairs of white corduroy shorts. I’m tapped out. I went through all the secret exits, my progress bar is a full 100%, and the only thing left for me to do this winter was to enjoy my cords. Just as I was settling into my Cordatorium, however, Banana Republic went ahead and released one of the best pairs of cords I’ve seen in years. So all of that planned restraint went out the window immediately.

It’s an unfortunate situation for a number of reasons, but each one of those is personal, and that’s what therapy is for. Otherwise, I couldn’t be happier because the Loose Pleated Corduroys are even better than I recklessly imagined.

Because they’re made from one of the most buttery, wide-ish wale corduroy fabrics I’ve seen a substantial brand use in ages, the first thing that you’ll notice about these is how soft they are, because, brother. They are soft. Like foam-pit-, down-pillow-, Jellycat-soft. But lots of things are soft, so let’s talk about the weight, which isn’t suffocating, but far heavier than most woven cotton fabrics— cozy as hell, sure, and weighted like a pair of vintage wool flannel trousers. As a result, the drape is fantastic and they hold their shape all day long.

And let’s talk about that shape. The straight-leg silhouette is inspired by vintage officer chinos—no year specified—which can be a pretty vague reference point. However, my favorite chinos on planet earth are a pair of OrSlow’s that are based on a model from the early-40s and these fit very close to those. They’re loose, with a high-ish waist and a straight leg that plays nice atop everything from boots to derbies to some daintier fare. And in regards to the pleat, it’s not overwhelming for those concerned about that kind of thing, but it also is very much part of the overall tapestry, which I appreciate; a deeper pleat (or multiples) can be a bit polarizing, but this one adds just the right amount of drama without becoming the focal point of the waistband.

Enough so, in fact, that these cords haven’t just cracked my rotation, they’ve been occupying a whole ass starter spot since they indicated up. (On this team, we reward performance with minutes. Those are the rules.) And considering it’s only getting chillier, things probably won’t change. I’ll be wearing them to more formal functions with a sweater and some Thiers; I’ll throw them on with my shittiest V-neck or T-shirt to go shoot pool for hours without fear of wayward chalk or spilled Miller (they’re machine washable); I’ll be wearing them in place of jeans to run errands (again, they’re warm); and for doing virtually anything else for the foreseeable future, because they’re just a really good pair of pants.

Sources indicate that so, if you’re feeding an irrepressible addiction like myself or just simply need a great pair of winter pants for less than $150, check these ones out. With that, my personal Cordatorium is booming again, and all I can hope for is that Banana stays quiet for the next few months.

Massie moves to force Hegseth impeachment vote

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1263 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday.
  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the issue could occur by Wednesday.
  • A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

According to recent reports, rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the issue could occur by Wednesday.

A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.

Massie's resolution also charges Hegseth with disregarding protection of civilians in wartime and suppressing the free speech of a U.S. senator.

Massie revealed his intention to file the resolution as a matter of the privileges of the House.

In a recent development, speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., will now have to rule as to whether the resolution constitutes a proper question of the privileges of the House. There is precedent from prior instances when impeachment was found to be valid as it relates to the House’s constitutionally granted powers.

He must schedule a vote to occur within two legislative days. Assuming that the speaker rules that Massie's resolution is privileged, the House could vote on the resolution itself, or on a motion to table it or refer it to committee.

If the House were to impeach Hegseth under this process, it would mark a historical anomaly. According to the Congressional Research Service, recent attempts to impeach an official as a matter of the privileges of the House have not resulted in approval of the resolution. In cases in which an official has been impeached, the House has nearly always chosen to conduct an investigation first.

In an interview on Oct. 26, Massie put the chances of his resolution being adopted at 50-50.

In comments to reporters outside the Capitol after his floor remarks, Massie stated he suspected some Republicans may back his resolution but he indicated he has neither asked for nor received any such assurances from any of them.

He predicted there could be some GOP support in the Senate if Hegseth is impeached and it goes to trial. He noted that if the trial does not start until 2027, any Republicans who might vote to convict Hegseth would presumably be joined by most if not all of a more sizeable Senate Democratic caucus.

Massie's odds of success for his resolution may now be greater than his previous 50-50 prediction given the results of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which gave Democrats control over both chambers in the next Congress — a vote motivated largely by opposition to the Iran war and its inflationary impact.

The questions now are, first, how many House Republicans will defy President Donald Trump and vote to impeach Hegseth; and, secondly, how many incumbents who lost their reelection bids on Nov. 3, a cohort that is disproportionately Republican, might be absent for the impeachment vote?

According to recent reports, massie remarked some Republicans who lost their reelection bids may feel freer to vote to impeach Hegseth. And he also said Republicans who were reelected and will have to face voters in 2028 may also think about how their vote on an impeachment resolution would reverberate politically.

"It's going to be everybody's conscience, and then they'll have to live with that vote," Massie remarked. "And they're going to have to live with that vote two years from now if they're not part of the retirement caucus. And if they were part of the retirement caucus, what do they have to lose?".

Asked why he did not bring articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump, Massie said: "I think the president needs to see one of — this is a metaphor — one of his horses shot out from under him, and then maybe he'll he will see things differently.".

If the House does vote on Massie’s resolution, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who is expected to become the House speaker in the next Congress, noted on ABC’s “This Week” on Sunday that he would be a “hard yes” on it.

Hegseth has “got to go,” Jeffries mentioned. “The so-called secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe.”.

Most if not all House Democrats are expected to agree.

Last week, Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., the ranking member of the Armed Services Committee and its likely chairman in the next Congress, indicated in an interview with The Newly introduced Republic that he would support Massie’s impeachment resolution, and he predicted it would be adopted.

Sources indicate that referring to Massie’s measure, Smith said, “By every estimation, it will pass and he will be impeached. And off that goes to the Senate. Then the Senate is legally required to spend all of their time dealing with that until it’s done with.”.

It has been revealed that "Every second Pete Hegseth remains at the top of the Pentagon, our servicemembers are at risk," Rep. Jason Crow, D-Colo., a senior member of the Armed Services Committee, remarked in a post on X on Sunday.

Also on Monday, Everett B. Kelley, the national president of the American Federation of Government Employees, a union that represents some 820,000 federal and D.C. government employees, sent a letter to House members urging a “yes” vote on Massie's Hegseth impeachment resolution.

The letter cited the risks Kelley said the Iran war has posed to the lives of the Defense Department's uniformed and civilian personnel, and the missive noted Hegseth's stripping of workplace rights and protections for the department's civilians.

It has been revealed that "By adopting Rep. Massie’s resolution, the House can begin the long overdue bipartisan effort to reclaim its constitutional powers and authority, restore checks and balances, and take responsibility for the lives of military personnel and civilian employees that Mr. Hegseth’s capricious leadership has jeopardized," Kelley wrote.

It has been revealed that massie announced in mid-September his intention to file an impeachment resolution against Hegseth. But Johnson adjourned the House before the vote would have occurred.

Massie’s fresh resolution is substantially the same as his earlier one, with the same eight articles of impeachment.

The first three of these alleges that Hegseth’s conduct of the Iran war violated the War Powers Resolution.

Massie's measure says Hegseth prosecuted the Iran war without congressional authorization and in the absence of an attack on the United States or an imminent threat.

Further, the measure alleges that Hegseth continued the war despite the House and Senate adopting in June a concurrent war powers resolution calling for the withdrawal of U.S. forces from the fight.

And, the resolution says, Hegseth continued the Iran war after the expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period.

Massie’s measure further asserts that Hegseth:.

Recent findings suggest that the House has only voted twice to impeach a member of the Cabinet. In 1876, Secretary of War William Belknap was impeached over allegations of corruption, and his abrupt resignation likely contributed to his acquittal in the Senate.

In 2024, the House voted 214-213 to impeach Alejandro Mayorkas, then-secretary of Homeland Security, for “willful and systemic refusal to comply with the law” and “breach of public trust.” The Senate dispensed with the charges without a trial.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • You can try XERF, swear by Therapeutic Plasma Exchange, or have your Golki bone-setting specialist on speed dial.
  • Sources indicate that “I think women can spend so much time looking for products to reverse signs of aging that they overlook the one product that can help prevent further damage,” she notes.
  • Whether mineral, chemical, or some combination of both, modern sunscreen formulas represent a shift from purely “protective” formulas into multitasking products that serve as skincare, notes Sandra Oska, MD, a board-certified dermatologist based in California.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You can try XERF, swear by Therapeutic Plasma Exchange, or have your Golki bone-setting specialist on speed dial. But behind every Dorian Gray-style complexion—even those that have benefitted from all those cutting-edge treatments, and then some—is a humble skin-care staple containing SPF 30 or above. According to Carol Eisenstat, MD, founder and medical director of boutique medspa Line Eraser MD, “You can invest in all the lasers, injectables, and skincare you want, but if you’re skipping sunscreen every morning, you’re working against yourself.” The best sunscreens for mature skin, Dr. Eisenstat says, not only protect results of the very in-office procedures she performs daily; they also preserve existing collagen and elastin.

Sources indicate that “I think women can spend so much time looking for products to reverse signs of aging that they overlook the one product that can help prevent further damage,” she notes. Luckily, in 2026 the SPF market is rife with elegant, sophisticated formulas that transform daily application from a chore into, dare I say, a treat. (Personally, I can almost feel my skin heaving a deep, contented sigh when I apply La Mer’s silky formula on the mornings I’m feeling particularly luxe.).

Whether mineral, chemical, or some combination of both, modern sunscreen formulas represent a shift from purely “protective” formulas into multitasking products that serve as skincare, notes Sandra Oska, MD, a board-certified dermatologist based in California. Made with thoughtful ingredients like hyaluronic acid, ceramides, squalane, and peptides, the SPF formulas dermatologists now recommend to their aging patients target dryness, dullness, and uneven tone, while providing the ever-key broad-spectrum UV protection.

With mature shoppers spoiled for choice, which formulas truly deserve a spot in your cart (not to mention, your beach bag)? Ahead, Vogue editors and dermatologists share the sunscreens they most recommend for aging skin. Sun safely!

What’s the best sunscreen for aging skin?

It has been revealed that because mature skin is more prone to dryness and sensitivity, Dr. Collins recommends seeking out a formula that not only provides broad-spectrum sun protection but nourishes the skin with hydrating and reparative ingredients. The sunscreens on this list, from dermatologist-approved brands such as Augustinus Bader, Alastin, and SkinCeuticals, check every box.

What to Look for in a Sunscreen for Mature Skin.

Sources indicate that “Skin can lose its ability to maintain moisture as we age, and mature skin often needs more hydrating skin-care products,” claims Jeanette M. Black, MD, a board-certified dermatologist and fellowship-trained cosmetic dermatologic surgeon. “This means that sunscreen itself should be more hydrating or be easily layered on top of a moisturizing cream.” (For instance, Roundlab Birch Juice Moisturizing UV Lock contains hyaluronic acid and the glycerin derivative glyceryl glucoside.) Dr. Black adds that any sunscreen should have an SPF 30 or higher and offer broad-spectrum protection.

Emme Diane Burg, an esthetician, skincare formulator, and the founder of Emme Diane Skincare, gives extra points to sunscreens that feature a PA+ to PA+++ on the label. “PA+++ is a grading system that focuses on UVA testing,” she states. “If you notice PA+ on your label, the product offers some protection against UVA rays, which are the ‘aging’ rays that cause damage and cancer. As the symbols increase, so does the level of UVA protection. So in this instance, the higher ratings, such as PA+++, are better in terms of sun protection,” she says.

Finally, a formula that’s fragrance-free, such as G.W.S. All-Over Sun Milk, is always a plus for mature skin. “In general, I recommend patients avoid sunscreens and other products with fragrances or other unnecessary ingredients that could potentially cause irritation,” Dr. Black states. And for patients of any age who are more active and might be exercising or swimming, she always recommends a water-resistant sunscreen.

Are chemical or mineral sunscreens best for mature skin?

“Mineral sunscreens are the safest and the only type of sunscreen that I recommend for not only safety concerns, but also their ability to block both UVA and UVB rays for broad-spectrum protection,” states Justine H. Park, MD, a board-certified dermatologist at Skin and Beauty Center in West Hills, California. Dr. Black adds: “Mature skin can mean that the skin is more sensitive, and for patients who might have potential sensitivities to the ingredients in chemical sunscreens, mineral sunscreen might be preferred.”.

However, Burg argues that chemical sunscreens can do more good than harm for mature skin. “Many people assume that mineral or physical sunscreens are inherently ‘non-toxic,’ while chemical sunscreens are ‘toxic’,” she says. “However, the reality is more nuanced. In certain situations—such as extended sun exposure or harsher outdoor conditions—a chemical sunscreen may offer more reliable protection. Physical sunscreens can be easily compromised if the protective barrier is inadvertently wiped away, for instance by sweat, friction from clothing, or even the straps of a backpack.” In short, she says, choosing between a chemical and mineral sunscreen should involve case-by-case analysis. For Burg herself, she oftentimes wears a mineral sunscreen on her face and a chemical sunscreen on her body, particularly if she’s spending time outside.

When we test and review a product, we take a holistic approach to deliver well-rounded product recommendations. First, we lean on Vogue's vast network of experts—from board-certified dermatologists to celebrity estheticians—to gain professional acumen on the industry's standout products, ones these specialists would actually use on their clients. We pair their expertise with our editorial best practices to curate the thoughtful edits you read on our site.

As it relates to retinol creams and serums, we selected the best based on the following characteristics: ingredients, texture, ease of application, packaging, finish, and the skin-care concerns they address. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, the best sweaters for men are, next to a hearty soup, the coziest, most comforting things of the colder seasons.
  • It has been revealed that consider what you’re trying to achieve with a sweater.
  • It has been revealed that like Michael Jordan dropping his famous “I'm back” statement, the V-neck is ready to reclaim its menswear throne as the MVP of your sweater rotation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, the best sweaters for men are, next to a hearty soup, the coziest, most comforting things of the colder seasons. And like a delicious bowl of life-giving soup, sweaters come in a myriad of styles, each with their own distinct combination of flavors, textures, and cultural significance. A classic merino wool crewneck sweater is the chicken noodle soup of the knitwear realm while a potato leek soup is more like a mohair turtleneck with its velvety, creamy texture. A hot bowl of thick, savory congee parallels the heavy-gauge knit and cold-busting insulation of a Cowichan cardigan. But whether it’s a quarter zip or menudo, cashmere or kimchi jjigae, navigating the endless amount of options can be tough, especially on an empty stomach.

It has been revealed that consider what you’re trying to achieve with a sweater. That can be both literal and metaphorical Are you trying to channel the GOAT decade, dripping in ’90s nostalgia? Or are you gearing up for holiday fits and festive chaos? Or maybe you just need a workhorse sweater that looks great with most outfits and will keep you warm three seasons out of the year. Whatever the case may be, you’ve come to the right place and while we can’t tell you what your palate will like, we can walk you through the menu.

It has been revealed that like Michael Jordan dropping his famous “I'm back” statement, the V-neck is ready to reclaim its menswear throne as the MVP of your sweater rotation. You might be tempted to start with the obvious play, like layering one over a crisp button-up shirt, maybe letting the shirt's collar laze insouciantly over the V. But follow the leads of the romcom stars and airport travel gods from the '90s: there’s something casually chic about a plain white T-shirt peeking out at clavicle height.

In a recent development, it's the Champion sweatshirt you wish you could live in, but refined enough to handle weekday meetings and weekend coffee dates. Crewneck sweaters can come in more flavors than Baskin-Robbins, and can be made from jacquard knits (see below), thick cable knits (also below), or damn near any other woven fabric. Our only suggestion: while there’s nothing wrong with a gets-the-job-done heather gray colorway, don't shortchange yourself by avoiding more adventurous colors.

According to recent reports, the sweater vest moment has been ramping up for several seasons and while we may be at peak vest, we're still totally here for it. It’s a notoriously tricky knit to style, but one that can actually add a ton of versatility to your closet. Whatever's underneath—a striped button-up shirt, a tee, nothing but your guns—gets a supporting actor nod. For extra warmth, the sweater vest fits well under both cropped outerwear and tailoring, like a suit jacket or sport coat, without adding unnecessary bulk. And it can turn a simple white tee-and-jeans combo (maybe add some loafers?) into an unstoppable farmers-market-to-cocktail-hour fit.

In a recent development, depending on the weather and your location's relation to the equator, a lightweight cardi will be the only “coat” you need. If temperatures are still moderately warm, opt for a cardigan made from breathable linen or cotton, paired with a button-up shirt and relaxed-fit chinos for a laid-back, preppy look. Once temps start to cool down, upgrade your winter wardrobe with a heavyweight wool sweater—maybe with a scarf-replacing shawl collar—to stay nice and toasty.

Industry observers note that whether you prefer a quarter-zip, half-zip, or full-zip, the knitwear of choice for dads all over is back. Look past its dorky nature and a zip sweater can be clean as a whistle and more stylish than you remember. Think of it as a convertible, but for your torso. Show off a little T-shirt and a necklace underneath, or zip that thing all the way to the top for a riff on the turtleneck that trades stuffy for sporty.

According to recent reports, it's a sweater with a collar, ya know what I mean? But in all seriousness, the polo sweater is even more solutions-oriented than its short-sleeve sibling. It instantly adds a touch of dressiness to an outfit without having to go full button down and tie, all while maintaining Olympic levels of cozy. Pair it with some non-jean pants for the easiest, comfiest Monday-through-Friday outfit in your arsenal. Or, let it anchor your out-of-office—the brighter and bolder, the better.

Blending form (straight lines to elongate that torso) with functionality (gotta keep ya neck warm) with sexiness (just look at it), the turtleneck remains a humble wardrobe heavyweight. A simple rib knit version can do damn near anything, anytime, but don't sleep on a turtleneck with a crochet, cable, or jacquard knit. Just ask The Rock, Michael B. Jordan, Tom Holland, or any of Hollywood's many leading men who figured out long ago that a turtleneck turns up the heat in more ways than the obvious.

The quintessentially preppy cable knit is the sweater most likely to say it “went to school in Cambridge.” You can lean into the Ivy League energy, or mix-and-match other styles. Similar, yet completely distinct, is the fisherman sweater or the Aran sweater. Originating from the western cost of Ireland, Aran sweaters have their roots in fishing and use intricate cable knit designs. A key difference aside from their origins is that fisherman sweaters are always hearty, chunky knits with thicker cable-knit designs.

It has been revealed that like the Aran sweater, the Fair Isle sweater is also named for an island (in the Shetlands, off the coast of Scotland). This time, the signature designs are less about texture, and more about the color, with traditional patterns knit into the wool. While it’s been unfairly dragged into the whole “Christmas sweater" conversation, Fair Isles deserve to be worn for as many months as you need the toastiness.

According to recent reports, as mentioned, you should go into this like you’re adopting a dog, not like a kid in a candy store. It can be satisfying for a moment to pick up the first pretty thing you see, but a crash follows the rush and before you know it, you’ve got a pile of sweaters that are either too warm, too itchy, or just don’t fit right. Don’t make that mistake, here’s what to look out for.

Cotton: We’re not going to belabor the benefits of cotton—the natural fiber is breathable, affordable, washes easily (though careful with the dryer—always read that tag), and gentle on sensitive skin. You can’t go wrong with a cotton sweater any time of the year, but if you’re looking for a transitional layer that’ll keep you warm now and comfortably cool later, it's hard to top cotton.

Recent findings suggest that wool: Not to mix our species, but wool can be a chameleon. The sheep-borne spectrum runs from airy and light to thick and hefty. But all of it is uniquely adept at regulating temperatures, so you'll stay warm without burning up. While you have to be a little more delicate on the upkeep (almost definitely no dryer), your tough-as-nails wool knit can last you for decades—literally—with some conscientious upkeep.

Cashmere: It used to be that the average “nice” wool sweater was made of merino wool or lambswool, and cashmere was reserved for the rich guys. A few decades of commodifying the luxury fiber has helped bring it to more affordable tiers. Though careful what you pay for: cheap cashmere pills easily, can feel oily, and won't last nearly as long as the good stuff.

Mohair: Shaggier and a hair (sorry) lighter than wool, a mohair sweater isn't afraid to make a statement. Chances are you’ve seen NBA elites sporting the ubiquitous horizontal-striped Marni cardigan, or you've spotted a number of Needle’s eyeball-popping patterned versions out in the wild. Though it's worth pointing out, you can absolutely find more relaxed versions—in both cardigan and button-free variations—if you're not trying to flex for ESPN's cameras.

Synthetics: More often than not, you’ll encounter sweaters that blend man-made materials like polyester, acrylic, and elastane. These materials can help give a sweater desirable qualities like softness, moisture-wicking, insulation, and stretch. They’re also cheaper to produce. While that doesn’t always translate into a low-quality product, it does mean that a brand is cutting costs which often result in an inferior garment.

Beyond the material that’s used to make a sweater, the yarns and gauge of those yarns influence light or heavy the final product will be. The fibers are spun into yarns, which are then knit together to form a sweater. The gauge refers to the thickness of those yarns and can be the difference between an airy spring sweater and a chunky deep-winter cardigan. The thicker the gauge, the heavier and warmer the sweater will be.

The balance between material and fabric weight is a delicate one. So when you’re deciding on a sweater, remember that a heavy cotton sweater can potentially be just as warm as a thin merino wool sweater or that a densely knit cashmere sweater will be warmer than an equally chunky cotton alternative.

According to recent reports, aside from the rarer summer knitwear, sweaters are made for cold weather. So fit is especially important considering you’ll be layering your sweater over and under other garments. Consider whether you’ll be wearing it over a button-up and tie or just a simple T-shirt. For the slightly reckless, slightly sexier among us, also consider whether you’ll be wearing it without any undershirt at all.

According to recent reports, same goes for the outer layers that’ll go on top. A chunky sweater is satisfying and cozy as hell, but can easily become unwieldy if you’re trying to stuff it under a tailored blazer. When it comes to fit, there’s no single best silhouette, but there are a couple of rules of thumb if you can’t make heads or tails of it. Make sure the shoulder seams hit just past your shoulder bones, that the sleeves reach to your wrist bones, and that the hem sits right around your hips.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that this is a Japanese-style rice porridge known as okayu. I ate this every morning in the early weeks of postpartum after my first daughter was born. It’s what our family reaches for whenever we need a simple, nourishing dish that warms from the inside out. For the smoothest porridge, let the rice soak in cold water before cooking.

According to recent reports, if you have time, soak the rice, which makes the texture softer and can aid in digestion. Place washed rice in a bowl and pour in water to cover by 1". Soak at least 30 minutes and up to 4 hours. Drain off excess water before starting the recipe. The wakame seaweed, which you’ve probably had in miso soup, can typically be found dried anywhere Asian groceries are available.

In a recent development, in The Fourth Trimester, we ask parents: What meal nourished you after welcoming your baby? This month it’s a cozy rice porridge by Eating at Home cookbook author Trinity Mouzon Wofford. Read more: Breakfast at Home, After Birth at Home.

It has been revealed that combine 1 cup short-grain rice, washed, soaked if desired, ¼ cup dried wakame (seaweed), 1 Tbsp. dried red shiso, and 6 cups low-sodium broth (any kind) or water in a large donabe, medium Dutch oven, or other heavy pot. Cover and bring to a boil over medium-high heat (you’ll hear bubbling). Uncover and stir, making sure nothing is stuck to bottom of pot. Cover and reduce heat to low. Continue to cook porridge 30 minutes more (resist the urge to peek).

Remove pot from heat and let porridge sit (still covered) 10 minutes. Uncover and stir. Rice grains should be cooked through, broken open, and creamy, but porridge should still be fairly loose. Season porridge with fine sea salt.

Ladle porridge into bowls and serve, topped with toasted sesame seeds, toasted sesame oil, and/or thinly sliced scallions.

Sources indicate that somewhere between Halloween and the holiday party bonanza, Friendsgiving has become fashion’s favorite excuse for a long and unhurried soirée. This year, hosts went all out with candlelit suppers, art gallery takeovers, and apartment hangouts a’plenty. Here’s a glimpse inside the rooms.

The holidays are off to a twinkling start, courtesy of jewelry designer Jessica McCormack and Net-a-Porter. An elegant Friendsgiving dinner saw both parties host a takeover of Salon 94 on the Upper East Side, with a finely decorated table and a mega-watt guest list.

In a recent development, sarah Paulson, Christy Turlington, Naomi Watts, Shalom Brune-Franklin, and Rebecca Henderson were among the crowd, along with clients, all ready to celebrate exclusive access to the celebrity-loved jewel’s pieces available on the e-tailer. (Christmas wish list, anyone?).

Sources indicate that A long table in The Stone Room was lined with low, lush runners of crimson dahlias, burnt-orange chrysanthemums, and inky calla lilies, punctuated by sprays of yellow orchids and tall taper candles. The three-course dinner included sea bass dressed in rainbow carrots, and a dessert of maple pumpkin pie with salted pecan brittle: a seasonal finale worth saving room for.

Recent findings suggest that for McCormack, the company mattered as much as the menu. “The best evenings are the ones that bring together an interesting, inspiring mix of people,” she mentioned, calling the night “the perfect way to spend an evening in one of my favorite cities.” Net-a-Porter CEO Heather Kaminetsky agreed: “The holiday season is such a special time to bring people together.” —Freya Drohan.

Sources indicate that if there was ever a match made in sartorial heaven, it would be Thom Browne and Mr Porter. To mark the debut of the designer’s exclusive capsule—a seventeen-piece collection of signature knit and quilted styles in festive hues and classic patterns—created in collaboration with the luxury retailer, a debonair group convened at George McNally’s fresh restaurant Faux in Tribeca.

Co-hosted by Browne and Mr Porter’s buying director Daniel Todd, the evening commenced in the restaurant’s checkered-floor subterranean cocktail lounge, where a coterie of tastemakers including Tramell Tillman, Isaac Cole Powell, Laufey, and Michael Hainey sipped dirty martinis and discussed their upcoming Thanksgiving aims.

It has been revealed that in a low-lit corner, Anna Toonk offered tarot readings as a nod to the hand-painted tarot-inspired tiles that lined the dining room above. To announce dinnertime, a brass trio from the Brooklyn Chamber Orchestra led the crowd upstairs with a musical procession, before guests settled in for generous platters of steak frites.

In a recent development, if any brand has earned the right to announce the start of pajama season, it’s Olivia von Halle. The luxury silk-loungewear label invited guests to dress in their nighttime finery to mark the end-of-year revelry over cocktails and a seated dinner in the private dining room of Le Veau d’Or, the beloved Upper East Side French bistro that has become near impossible to snag a reservation at.

Creative director Gabriella Khalil co-hosted the evening, which spotlighted the label’s playful yet polished sensibility. Among those who ‘slipped into something a little more comfortable’ for the occasion were Tina Leung, Marjon Carlos, Jessica Wang, Melanie Grant, Vogue’s Lisa Aiken, Christina Grasso, and Chloe Crane-Leroux.

Industry observers note that after getting warmed up over festive tipples, the group sat down to a bespoke menu served family-style. Think: platters of steak au poivre and market fish, followed by decadent chocolate profiteroles. —Freya Drohan.

Recent findings suggest that is Friendsgiving the definitive holiday pregame? Actor and director Jordan Firstman certainly made the case in true Club Kid fashion with the help of Substack and A24.

Hosted in the actual Lower East Side apartment featured in the buzzy film, the evening gathered editors, writers, creatives, and Firstman’s inner circle for an intimate, home-cooked feast.

It has been revealed that warm air wafted from the oven upon entering the apartment, mingling with the autumnal breeze drifting in from the slightly open windows in the pre-war home. Martinis were stirred, not shaken; wine—a Tuscan red and a light-bodied white—and mead from Honey’s flowed; and Firstman’s drink of choice, Diet Coke, took residence in the ice-filled bathtub playing the role of cooler for the evening.

On the candlelit table lay intentionally broken loaves of rustic olive focaccia and crumbling wheels of Parmesan, framing a smorgasbord of radicchio salad, porchetta, roasted honeynut squash spread atop a bed of pistachio pesto, and towering platters of saucy meatballs, alongside a heartfelt nod to the film in the form of al dente bucatini tossed in red sauce.

Industry observers note that guests promptly twirled noodles onto ceramic plates before raising their glasses in a toast led by Substack’s head of entertainment Alison Werner and Firstman himself, setting the tone for a remarkable night among a chosen family full of vibrant cultural voices. For dessert? A rich chocolate mousse, served with dollops of hand-whipped cream or caramelized hazelnut topping.

Though the homemade spread was undeniably decadent, top billing was rightfully reserved for the conversation and unadulterated community as attendees lounged on plush sofas, lingered near the dining table, and roamed about the apartment to meet one another, catch up—or, as they say in the scene, kiki. —Edgar Gatsinzi.

Pamela Anderson and Pandora amplified the lush, garden-like interiors of Palma restaurant in Manhattan’s West Village, transforming the beloved neighborhood Italian spot into a candlelit floral wonderland for a heartfelt Friendsgiving celebration.

The entire restaurant was reserved for the occasion, with rows of long tables dressed in pink peonies, garden roses, flickering candles, and boxes of Pandora necklaces. Festivities began in the front bar, where guests mingled over floral-inspired cocktails and mocktails before gathering for an intimate plant-based feast. Throughout the space, romantic floral arrangements and Pandora jewelry displays added to the warm, garden-party atmosphere, and guests were also able to personalize necklaces with custom engravings.

The entirely vegan menu featured recipes straight from Anderson’s cookbook, I Love You: Recipes from the Heart, with dishes drawn from her family favorites. From creamy pumpkin risotto to crispy portobello Milanese, each course surprised guests, but the crowd favorite seemed to be the decadent sourdough gingerbread Guinness cake.

It has been revealed that “Pandora is like family,” Anderson told Vogue. “We’ve been together for three years now, and they’ve been such supporters of this stage in my career.” Expressing her gratitude for the brand and taking in the evening’s dreamy setting, she added, “They’ll go to the ends of the earth. I’m living inside my cookbook right now.”.

As the evening came to a close, guests left with a little piece of Anderson’s world: a sourdough starter kit to bring her love of home cooking into their own kitchens, along with lip balm from her beauty brand, Sonsie.

For Anderson, this Friendsgiving celebration was ultimately about “creating memories and creating fresh traditions,” surrounded by lush flowers, friends, and good food. —Donna Kim.

Sources indicate that friendsgiving is usually something of a misnomer when it comes to brands hosting dinner parties in the weeks leading up to Thanksgiving. Such was not the case at Urban Jürgensen’s night out, which was, quite literally, a Thanksgiving feast, complete with turkey, stuffing, cornbread, and cranberry sauce, all served around one long, convivial dinner table that could have given Norman Rockwell a run for his money.

Leading the resurrection of Urban Jürgensen, the revered watchmaker founded in 1773 that lay dormant until its revival in 2025, is CEO Alex Rosenfield, who played the role of consummate host. Welcoming guests to the upper floors of Pace Gallery in Chelsea, Rosenfield ensured the evening was imbued with all the warmth and charm of the places he holds dear, particularly those in and around his Sag Harbor home. This included a dinner menu devised by Shelter Island eatery Léon 1909, as well as the décor overhead: a hulking arrangement of autumn foliage plucked from trees in Sagaponack and transported into the city that very morning for assembly.

Industry observers note that with this in mind, Rory Satran, the former Wall Street Journal editor turned founder of The Hamptons Chronicle, a “mischievous local print newspaper” distributed along Long Island’s South Fork, was a natural choice for co-host. “I laugh when people say, ‘What’s your distribution plan?’ and it’s just me in my Volvo,” Satran told guests. “This past summer was great, and it couldn’t be done without incredible partners and friends, and Alex and his team are very much a part of that, as well as all of you here. I could go around and do shout-outs to all of you, but that would be super awkward, but you are all special to me.”.

Joining Satran around the table were Misha Kahn, Beverly Nguyen, Matthew Foley, Sophie Elgort, newly minted Vanity Fair columnist Chris Black, and vintner Joey Wölffer, who, like Satran, is a devout Hamptonite helping usher in a renewed appreciation for the charms of the East End that endure beyond its summertime glitz.

Industry observers note that “There’s something so special about the Hamptons that you can’t really explain,” Wölffer told Vogue. “You just feel it. Everyone around this table feels that too, and that’s what makes this so magical. I love how Rory celebrates the Hamptons through the Chronicle, and clearly Urban Jürgensen values the importance of the community. I think the food is a star tonight, too, though, I mean, come on.” —Zachary Weiss.

Jewelry designer Jenny Bird and Lipstick on the Rim co-host Emese Gormley recently toasted to female founders during a picture-perfect night at San Vicente in the West Village.

There was much cause for celebration as the pair hosted a serene evening at the members’ club: Gormley’s new perfume brand, Anyu, and her collaboration with Jenny Bird on the Anyu Baguette Signet Ring. (The striking piece, available in yellow or white gold, has a sentimental story behind it. Its name comes from the Hungarian word for “mother,” and it’s the content creator’s tribute to her own mother.).

Sources indicate that fittingly for an evening honoring a new business, the guest list was full of those who’ve successfully built their own in the worlds of fashion, lifestyle, and wellness. Around the table, the likes of Dria Murphy, Larissa Mills, Daphne Oz, and Julia McGuire all joined the hosts to raise a glass.

How the ‘blue tsunami’ crested in North Carolina

💡 Key Takeaways

  • LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that north Carolina Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack talks to reporters Sunday at the AC Hotel in Washington as she arrives for fresh member orientation. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.

But as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep. Tim Moore, the influential former speaker of the North Carolina House and a chief architect of the gerrymander that aimed to keep the 14th District safely red.

“There were a lot of pins and needles,” remarked Womack, a 49-year-old ordained minister who works at a Charlotte-based nonprofit. After seeing long lines at polling places extend into Election Day, she grew more confident: “People were ready to exercise their voice.”.

Womack – who raised less than $60,000 to Moore’s $2.1 million – eked out a 2-point win in the district, which reaches from the Charlotte suburbs to mountain counties in the west.

Saddled with an unpopular president and broad dissatisfaction with the status quo, Republican incumbents across the nation experienced a midterm drubbing last week. As of Monday evening, House Democrats had netted 42 seats, with more races left to be called. The GOP in North Carolina, a state that Trump carried three times, was among the hardest hit.

Democrats have so far flipped five House seats in the Tar Heel State. Besides Womack, the “blue tsunami” also swept in Paul Barringer, a lawyer who founded an outdoor clothing line, and High Point Mayor Cyril Jefferson. And Army veteran Richard Ojeda, who once served in the West Virginia Senate, defeated Rep. Richard Hudson, the chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee.

In a recent development, democrats also won two races that had been seen as competitive for much of the cycle. Farmer Jamie Ager flipped an open seat in the state’s mountain west, while Rep. Don Davis held on to his Eastern North Carolina district, which Republicans had redrawn in their favor.

Meanwhile, in the state’s hilly northwest corner, 11-term Republican Virginia Foxx, the chairwoman of the powerful Rules Committee, is fighting for her political future: As of Monday afternoon, former journalist Chuck Hubbard led her by 99 votes in the 5th District, though The Associated Press had yet to call the race.

It has been revealed that that was also true in the neighboring 10th District, where GOP incumbent Pat Harrigan had a 1-point edge over Democratic physician associate Ashley Bell. Also uncalled were a pair of contests in Eastern North Carolina, where Republican Rep. Greg Murphy clung to a 233-vote edge over Democratic former state Rep. Raymond Smith and GOP Rep. David Rouzer led Democratic social worker Kimberly Hardy by less than a point.

“Nobody could have predicted this,’’ said David Wilson Brown, who leads the Democratic Party in Gaston County near Charlotte and has lost two bids for the House, including to Foxx in 2020. “It’s a watershed moment.”.

The Democratic rout in the midterm elections was powered by victories in states with new GOP-favored maps, including Texas, Ohio and Florida.

Sources indicate that but Democrats’ success in North Carolina was especially striking given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Since Republicans flipped the state legislature in 2010, and with it control of the redistricting process, no House GOP incumbent had lost a general election in the Tar Heel State until last week.

This year’s  congressional map – the state's sixth in seven election cycles – was engineered by the Republican-led legislature to help the party capture 11 of the state's 14 House seats.

It has been revealed that but the Democratic surge was so big that it easily overpowered the GOP’s built-in edge. Democratic candidates were also lifted by former Gov. Roy Cooper, whose 20-point Senate win provided the underticket with powerful coattails.

Industry observers note that “In order for them to gerrymander our state in the way that they did, they were spread very thin,” Brown noted, referring to state Republicans. “So they were kind of ripe to be defeated that way.”.

The repeated rounds of redistricting may have also erased some of the advantages of incumbency, according to Peter L. Francia, a political science professor at East Carolina University. “If you carve up a district every two years, you've taken away some of that [advantage]. And I think that that came back and hurt Republicans in this cycle.”.

Doug Heye, a GOP strategist and a former spokesman for the Republican National Committee, mentioned redistricting “ticked off a whole lot of voters, and really activated the Democratic base.”.

On the Republican side, voters were “less motivated because they were unexcited about Trump,’’ Heye added.

Republican incumbents accustomed to winning by comfortable margins weren’t prepared for a political environment driven by anger over the war in Iran and angst about the rising cost of living.

According to recent reports, “Clearly, a lot of those Republicans didn’t take their elections seriously,” Heye said. “They won last time with 18 points. They weren't on anyone's radar screen, so they didn't think they had to do anything.”.

Sources indicate that womack credits her win to a grassroots campaign centered on economic issues. While her race wasn’t on the national radar – Moore, after all, won by 16 points in 2024 – and her campaign didn’t have money for ads, she was out in the district doing events every day.

According to recent reports, “There are a lot of working families right now who are in the missing middle,” she said in an interview. “They make too much money to get help, but they don't make enough money to get ahead. … Someone who can be working a full-time job, but still doesn’t have enough money to buy groceries or to afford their medications or to have access to health insurance.”.

Womack said her own struggles have shaped her approach to politics. This week, she’s slated to appear in court on a felony charge for allegedly failing to return a rental car in 2019. The incident wound up in one of Moore’s attack ads.

Recent findings suggest that “There are so many people who [understand] what happens when you're down on your luck and you don't have enough money to make good financial decisions,’’ she said. “Most people don't want those bad decisions to be a definition of their character for the rest of their life.”.

Early in the midterm cycle, Democratic opposition research group American Bridge prepared detailed dossiers on Republican House incumbents in North Carolina.

Industry observers note that “Someone like Virginia Foxx, she’s been on the Hill forever,” said Pat Dennis, the group’s president. “She was somebody … who under the radar could be vulnerable. So we started really early.”.

Recent findings suggest that american Bridge’s political arm spent $340,000 on ads targeting Foxx. One spot featured a man who identified himself as a Trump voter expressing anger at the government’s response to Hurricane Helene, which devastated the mountain communities of Western North Carolina two years ago.

Other Democrats scoffed at the group’s decision to spend money targeting entrenched Republicans far from the main House battleground.

“There was a lot of reluctance from people to really believe that that data was correct, but it was,’’ Dennis said. “Then over the summer, we saw her numbers collapsing, so we put paid media behind it and it really paid off.”.

Hubbard ran against Foxx two years ago and lost by almost 20 points.

“I kind of had a notion I was going to do this again,’’ he stated in an interview Saturday while en route to Washington for freshman orientation. “I don’t like to lose at checkers, much less a congressional race.”.

After a court-drawn map resulted in a split North Carolina delegation after the 2022 elections, state Republicans won back control of the map-making process and went on to win 10 of the state’s 14 House seats under a upcoming map two years later.

At Trump’s urging, Republicans made further tweaks to the North Carolina map last year, but the original gerrymander finally came back to bite the GOP in 2026, according to Hubbard.

It has been revealed that “North Carolina is one of the most severely gerrymandered states,’’ he noted. “And what happened was they had to steal from Peter to pay Paul. It's been referred to by political scientists as a dummymander.”.

As the vote count in the 5th District continues, Foxx, whose campaign declined to comment for this story, has requested the presence of nonpartisan election observers.

They “will serve as key, watchful eyes to ensure that this sacred process is not impeded and that all legal votes are counted in a consistent, thorough manner,’’ she posted on social media.

But even before the final races are called, Republicans are already looking to the next election.

Heye, who expects North Carolina to remain a purple state in 2028 and beyond, cautioned the Democrats who won last week not to get too comfortable in Washington. He invoked Fred Heineman, the former Raleigh police chief who rode the 1994 “Republican Revolution” to Congress – and lasted a single term.

“Some of them will lose, and some of the people who lost may run two years from now and get their seat back,’’ he mentioned.

One GOP operative, who requested anonymity to speak candidly, offered up a similar assessment.

Trump “didn't keep his promises” and that “just got voters very angry and suppressed the GOP base from coming out because, in a midterm election it's a base turnout contest,’’ the strategist noted.

“But these Democrats are renting these districts for two years.”.

Well, there was a quick power nap somewhere around 5 a.m., but otherwise I've been working very hard. I have a new wardrobe and some concerns about the price of digital jorts.

Sources indicate that most people will have spent their first-ever session getting through the missions, exploring the map, and finding out what Jason and Lucia have got themselves into. Not me. My main goal was to visit as many shops as possible. It's been 13 years since GTA 5; I wanted to see what had happened to the menswear.

Before we get into it, you should know: Your in-game clothes matter more than ever compared to other entries in the Grand Theft Auto universe. As I wrote last week, the new “heat” system lets cops remember what you were wearing, so losing them doesn't necessarily mean you're in the clear. Changing your hat or sunglasses won't clear the clothing clue, either. You need a full fit change. So technically, all this shopping could help me get away with something. That's my justification, anyway.

In a recent development, unfortunately, even virtual shopping requires cold, hard cash—and early on, that takes considerably more effort than I'd hoped. You start with almost nothing, spending much of the opening stretch around Key Lento in swampy Mariana County. I'd gone in expecting to buy loads of clothes. Instead, I was checking what I could afford.

Industry observers note that my first opportunity came in a random gun shop that also sold some workwear. I had a quick browse then went straight for the camo shorts. Back in August, British GQ's senior style editor Mahalia Chang declared that “camo shorts are fucking back, baby,” having watched Jason spend much of the trailer wearing them. Who was I to argue?

According to recent reports, nearby, in Hamlet, I found a few thrift shops and picked up a battered chore jacket with more than a little Carhartt Detroit about it. It looked properly used, which suited both my budget and the general condition of my pickup. I bought a watch, too, but more on that another time.

I was already getting quite into it. I was comparing pieces, checking prices, and deciding what could wait. There were clothes I wanted and clothes I could afford. Annoyingly, the game understood the difference.

Recent findings suggest that I bought a trucker cap at one point and was very happy with it. Over the summer, I wrote about wanting to give them another go despite having a head my mates call “a sniper's dream.” Jason doesn't have that problem (in a metaphorical sense, anyway), so I thought I'd let him enjoy one. Shortly afterwards, a gang of lads picked a fight with me, punched me, and knocked it off his head. I fled, only realizing once I was safely away that I hadn't picked it back up. I'd barely had a chance to enjoy it. I hope one of them's wearing it at least.

After a few missions, I finally had enough money to justify another shopping trip. I got into my beaten-up pickup and headed downtown, where the prices started getting a little more serious. Denim jackets were around $120. A pair of dark wash jorts I really liked cost $45, which was slightly more than I wanted to spend.

Recent findings suggest that I appreciate that this is a game in which you can steal a car, and I was still having a small financial discussion with myself about the price of shorts. For a game called Grand Theft Auto, I'd done surprisingly little car stealing in the time I'd been playing.

It has been revealed that the map is absolutely massive, and there almost 70 clothing stores to work through, so visiting everything was never gonna happen in one sitting. Cars now use fuel, too. Driving miles out of your way to look at a jacket comes with an additional expense, and I had to leave enough money to get home.

According to recent reports, there was a reason to keep exploring, though. I went into another shop expecting more of the same and realized the stock was different, so now I wanted to check the other shops before buying anything. Apparently, I'd waited 13 years to recreate how I spend my Saturdays.

Naturally, I decided to drive to Ocean Beach, a more expensive part of the city where I had very little business shopping. Inside Nola, the person at the till looked me up and down in my shitty workwear and asked, “Eh, are you looking for somebody?”.

Industry observers note that it was an impressively efficient assessment of my finances. Nola felt a little like Casablanca, the French-Moroccan label known for colorful prints, sportswear, and clothes that suggest a considerably nicer holiday than the one you're on. I'd previously called Hawaiian shirts “the unofficial uniform of Vice City.” Here, joining in cost about $330. Blazers were about $430. I could look, provided I didn't get any dirt on anything.

Recent findings suggest that then I accidentally punched the shop assistant; I'm still getting used to the controls. At least, I think it was an accident. Either way, I had to flee before I could give the blazers much consideration. When I came back later, the store was temporarily closed. I hope it wasn't due to staff injuries.

Other boutiques were even less accommodating to my balance. Italian house Ferruccio Tucci (probably a GTA-ified Emilio Pucci) had $3,000 suits and $1,200 horsebit loafers. I went in to browse and accidentally bought a pair of $350 shades, which was a very expensive way to learn which button does what. The annoying thing is that they looked genuinely sick—exactly the sort of thing I'd wear IRL, which made it much easier to justify keeping them. Well, that was fuel and dinner gone for the day. At least I could look good while walking home.

Later, driving past Waxman Island, I came across Vice City's Eris flagship. Obviously, I had to go in. For anyone who hasn't spent the past few months staring at fictional trainers, Eris is basically GTA's answer to Nike. Nike takes its name from the Greek goddess of victory; Eris is the goddess of strife and discord. The shoes are often just as recognizable as the joke.

Sources indicate that the store kinda reminded me a little of Niketown in London—right now closed for refurbishment—with neon lights and big statues and enough footwear to keep me occupied considerably longer than was sensible. There was the Rise Low, an Air Force 1 lookalike that I ended up getting in two colourways; the Strife 360, with its very Air Max 97-ish shape; and the Rook 1 High, which follows the Air Jordan 1 High. I own more than 400 pairs of sneakers IRL—I probably should've known that going in here would be a problem.

And Eris is only one option. There are alternative sneaker labels, beach shops, souvenir shops, and smaller, DIY-looking streetwear brands all dotted around the city. I'd barely begun working through them. Every time I thought I'd seen enough to stop, there was another shop worth going into.

Industry observers note that the most expensive-looking thing I acquired didn't come from a boutique at all. Slight spoiler: A naked man offered to give me his “Crowex” watch after pulling a plastic egg out of his own ass. (Yes, you read that right.) You'll know him when you see him. I'm not gonna go into any more detail, partly because I'm tired and partly because I'd like you to experience that transaction yourself.

It has been revealed that eight hours in, I'd hardly scratched the surface. What surprised me most was how long the expensive stuff felt like it would take to earn. Those suits and loafers were sitting there, available to try, while my balance suggested another few missions first. There's a lot of city left to explore, quite a few shops I want to revisit, and a pair of jorts I'm still thinking about.

Sources indicate that for now, though, I need some sleep. And Jason needs to earn back that $350.

A version of this story originally appeared in British GQ.

#180548. Tech Report: Apple Juice Bread

📅 22 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (711 w)

Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Epicurious ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: Apple Juice Bread

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Epicurious

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level.
  • I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal.
  • Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A simple swap from water to apple juice transforms this basic bread recipe into a subtly sweet loaf that is perfect to tear into at breakfast time with a smear of good butter on top, but it also takes a PB&J to the next level. The subtle, but unmistakable, undercurrent of apple sweetness struck me as a bit of a magic trick in a bread that, otherwise, to the eye and hand was just a soft white loaf.

I first encountered the idea at the small four-seat teppanyaki restaurant in the back of the Suiran Hotel in Kyoto, Japan, where chef Tsubasa Yamaguchi served it before my first course; it was a perfect way to start the meal. When I asked him what he did differently to prepare it, he stated he just took the same rustic bread recipe he baked elsewhere and used apple juice in place of water. I was incredulous. That was it? The same amount? The same technique? Yes and yes, he said. I was hooked. It turns out the water-to-juice switcheroo gives an added taste of fall without taking anything away from the shape and texture. It’s become an instant favorite at my house both breakfast and lunch, and I expect it will be at yours.

Take care when you’re lowering the bread into the Dutch oven; it is a slightly nerve-wracking moment but a little attention is all that’s needed. You can do it!

More apple recipes here: 37 Apple Desserts That Make Us Want to Pick the Whole Orchard.

It has been revealed that mix 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, 1¾ cups apple juice, 1 Tbsp. Diamond Crystal or 1¾ tsp. Morton kosher salt, 1 Tbsp. sugar, and one ¼-oz. envelope instant yeast (about 2¼ tsp.) in a large bowl just until flour is hydrated and a very shaggy dough forms, about 1 minute. Cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit at room temperature 15 minutes.

In a recent development, set a small bowl of room-temperature water on work surface for easy reaching. Uncover dough, dip your hand in water and stretch one side of dough up and over to meet opposite side; turn bowl 90°. Repeat 3 more times, turning bowl 90° after each fold. (This constitutes 1 full fold.) If dough doesn’t always stretch to meet opposite side, just aim for the middle. Wet your hands and shake off excess water any time dough begins to feel sticky. Cover dough and let sit 30 minutes (set a timer). Repeat folding process to make 1 full fold. Re-cover and let dough sit another 30 minutes. Repeat folding process and resting one more time. By the last fold, dough should be significantly smoother and tighter.

Industry observers note that transfer dough to a generously floured surface, dust with flour, and shape into a tight ball. Dust dough with more flour. Dust a kitchen towel with flour and place inside a high-sided bowl to line. Arrange dough, seam side up, in bowl on top of towel. Tightly cover bowl with plastic wrap and let dough sit in a warm spot until puffy, about 45 minutes.

Place a rack in middle of oven, then set a large ovenproof Dutch oven with a lid on it; preheat oven to 400°. Place a 12" square of parchment paper on a flat surface. Cut a 2"-long slit in each corner toward the center. Very carefully, tip dough out onto center of parchment, trying your best not to deflate it or ruin its shape. (It’s easiest to place parchment on a flat plate so you can easily turn dough out of bowl.) Working very quickly and using a pair of kitchen shears lightly coated in vegetable oil, cut an X in center of bread. Remove pot from oven and very carefully lower dough into pot. Cover pot and return to oven.

According to recent reports, bake bread 35 minutes. Uncover pot, reduce oven temperature to 375°, and continue to bake bread until crust is deeply browned, 35–40 minutes more. Carefully tip loaf out onto a wire rack and let cool at least 1 hour before slicing.

Do Ahead: Bread can be baked 3 days ahead. Let cool completely; store airtight at room temperature.

#180545. The Real-Life Wardrobe of Michael Bennett, Who Traded the NFL for Furniture Design

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2116 w)

The Real-Life Wardrobe of Michael Bennett, Who Traded the NFL for Furniture Design

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2116 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When you’ve won a Super Bowl ring, made three Pro Bowl appearances, and played a key role on one of the most dominant defensive squads ever—the Seattle Seahawks’ 2010s-era Legion of Boom—what do you do next?
  • After completing his 11-year NFL career in 2020, the 41-year-old enrolled at two institutions—the University of Hawaii and Seattle’s Heritage School of Interior Design—to study architecture and interior design, respectively.
  • Through his design practice Studio Kër, Bennett debuted an 11-piece collection of avant-garde furniture inspired by the African diaspora in 2024, which was well received by critics.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When you’ve won a Super Bowl ring, made three Pro Bowl appearances, and played a key role on one of the most dominant defensive squads ever—the Seattle Seahawks’ 2010s-era Legion of Boom—what do you do next? For Michael Bennett, the answer was to head back to school.

After completing his 11-year NFL career in 2020, the 41-year-old enrolled at two institutions—the University of Hawaii and Seattle’s Heritage School of Interior Design—to study architecture and interior design, respectively. “I’m a student of whatever I do,” Bennett tells me. “My best quality—and probably my worst quality—is that the things I love to do, I try to become the best. I play tennis five days a week. I’m trying to go to Wimbledon. And design and architecture are like that.”.

All that effort is paying off. Through his design practice Studio Kër, Bennett debuted an 11-piece collection of avant-garde furniture inspired by the African diaspora in 2024, which was well received by critics. He’s now hard at work on his sophomore line, alongside a spoken-word album and the occasional bespoke garment.

That last side quest should come as no surprise, because Bennett has some of the most distinctive personal style I’ve ever seen on a pro athlete–current or former—with a particularly clean headwear and accessories game. Here, Bennett tells me all about the skills he carried over from football into his newly introduced career, what fatherhood has taught him about masculinity, and the song he listens to every day.

In a recent development, michael Bennett: I’ve been playing football my whole life, man. After winning so much, I dug deep. I had already conquered the body. How do I conquer the mind? At what point am I being selfish? I’m missing so much of my kids’ lives. I’ve already been to the highest of the high. Am I going to leave my family with a broken man? That was really the question. Am I chasing ego or am I chasing something else? In reality, a lot of us are just chasing the ego, to be remembered, scared of the death of what [your life] was rather than [embracing] the growth that can be.

People want to keep others in a certain box because that’s the way that they understand them. That’s in any relationship. If you started to date somebody when they’re 20 and you turn 40 and they start to change, you’d be like, “You used to like your eggs like that.” People don’t allow others to transition; won’t allow people to actually experience growth. Often you’re meeting people in a time where they’re just starting to learn who they are. Over time you start to really develop who you are.

It has been revealed that the truth is it doesn’t matter if people take you seriously, [as long as] you take yourself seriously. What are you doing to practice your craft? Artists are like, “Oh, my practice, my practice.” I never really understood what that meant until I started doing my own practice. I practiced on the field and I can practice the body. But really, if you want to be taken seriously intellectually, then you have to practice the mind. Sometimes practicing the mind is also connected to the body. In football, yeah, you are connected to the mind in a certain way. But it isn’t always like learning to be a lawyer or an architect or an artist—to be a thinker, you’re doing something completely different. And it’s just allowing yourself to transition. Man, truthfully, you got to say fuck everybody.

In a recent development, I think it’s one of the most intellectual sports in general. Tennis is one of those sports where it’s about the angle, the quick twitch. You’re by yourself. With football, it’s the amount of moving parts. People overlook the amount of detail that it takes to run a team—practicing and going through a play 3,000 times before you actually get it. The best players I ever met were the smartest when it came to the sport. They were the PhDs of their craft.

It’s taught me vulnerability. It made me a better human. In some ways, my daughters have allowed me to mature. The sport of football requires so much masculinity. I’m not saying that all masculinity is toxic, [but] it’s more about, how do you hunt but still be gentle? The true samurai doesn’t strike, but knows he can.

Sources indicate that what my daughters have allowed me to do is develop my whole humanity. To have a daughter is so special—women are very special. As an athlete, people come back from injuries, but to see a woman come back from giving birth is a whole other level of love. My daughters have been my greatest accomplishments in my life. I never made a Super Bowl trophy. There’s always another winner. But there’s only one Peyton, there’s only one Blake, and there’s one Ollie. As a maker, those are the most special things that I could make.

In a recent development, in 2019, I was really into Booker T. Washington and W.E.B. Du Bois and [their debate over] the “Talented Tenth.” [Booker T. Washington believed that] intellectualism should never get away from the idea of making. I got into design because I’ve always been involved in politics, and politically, I started to realize that everything came down to design.

Recent findings suggest that shirt and pants by Studio Kër. Shoes by Collegium.

Sources indicate that whenever I spoke out about police brutality or on critical issues in America, that was really where I started to think about design as this language—this form of resistance. How can I change the system? It starts with design. Where I grew up, a non-gentrified area that was low income, it’s like you could see that there was no empathetic way of thinking about design. The definition of architecture for me is empathy for space. That’s what led me to this idea of these African diaspora forms and languages that I will use as my form of resistance.

I’m working on a latest collection of furniture. The first collection I did was called “We Gotta Get Back to the Crib,” which to me was really about getting back to the essence of Blackness. A lot of times we talk about Blackness and it’s always connected to traumatic experience. But to me, it was more about how can I connect to these true levels of love, these things really shaped my culture, my family, my mother, my grandmother, and everything that was beautiful about being Black? This next collection is about African brutalism. How can I bring these things that are seen in the ghetto in America and in West Africa and then turn those into ideas about furniture? A lot of times what I’m dealing with as a designer is this idea of abstraction. How can I pull and reference something in such a sweet way? Like how Virgil designed shoes with references, leaving crumbs to this unspoken past. As a designer, that’s what I’m trying to do.

Yeah, I got a spoken word project.

According to recent reports, as an athlete, if you talk about your cars or you talk about your jewelry, the way that you gained it doesn’t have that kind of Jay-Z effect—you didn’t hustle to get that. You played to get that, which is different from somebody hustling to get that. With spoken word, I think about Gil Scott-Heron or The Last Poets. They’re talking about critical complications. My perspective is really about humanizing the Black experience and the Black man. My stories and what I’m trying to tell with this music, E-Nigg-Ma, is so much about Black culture, Black design, Black features, this idea of what America is trying to suffocate about Blackness and not let it breathe.

Industry observers note that cuff by Dries van Noten. Ring by Olithica. Watch by Patek Philippe.

In a recent development, music. When I’m designing, beautiful sounds are really crucial to the way that I think. My number-one song that I always listen to is Miles Davis’s “Flamenco Sketches.” It’s my daily listen. Those are the sounds that I need to hear: the horn, the riffs, the in-between.

My studio inspires me, just the way light hits. It’s the simplest things. Seeing my family movies. My wife inspires me with what she’s designing.

Sources indicate that my great-grandpa, Hall Mack, everybody talked about his fashion. People still talk about his style. He was the first person I saw dry cleaning everything. His style was impeccable. When I look back at a period of style that I liked, it’d be the years of the Birth of the Cool. People like Miles, Sidney Poitier, everybody was just fresh.

I’ve always been connected to style. People always call me “Runway Mike.” They say, “Bro, you wear more Margiela than anybody I know.” I design my own clothes. [Style] is a part of who you are. I love the idea of fashion. I want to design a fashion show. Yo, Wales Bonner, let me design something for you! I want to be backstage.

According to recent reports, over time I just found me. That takes so much time. I feel like one of the most beautiful things is Instagram and this ability to share things, but one of the worst things is Instagram and the ability to share things. Because there’s a part of us that starts to mimic [what we see] in a way that isn’t true to us. We start to judge ourselves on other people’s experience.

In a recent development, sitting courtside, the Dune star wore a combination familiar to just about anyone who’s endured winter on the East Coast. This time out, he left the handbag at home but topped things off with a Knicks championship hat.

But these pull-ons were, in fact, from menswear favorite Merrell, built for some truly cold and ugly weather. The outer suede is water-resistant, the lining is insulated, and the rubber outsoles boast some serious traction. Plus, the very gorp-y utility cord at the heel lets you cinch them extra tight. Like the advanced-level dresser he is, Chalamet tucked his baggy black pants into the boots, making sure his footwear got a chance to really shine.

In a recent development, once again, Chalamet has turned practical winter clothes into an A-list look. While a pink puffer might not be every guy’s idea of cold-weather dressing, there’s something to be remarked for a winter coat with a little personality. Was celebrity row’s resident heartthrob a few weeks early with this ensemble? Sure, but when that first serious snowfall hits, he’ll be extra ready.

Recent findings suggest that season 1¼ lb. skinless, boneless chicken thighs (4–5) all over with 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt.

Transfer chicken to a cutting board and let cool slightly. Reduce heat to low and cover pot. Using 2 forks, shred chicken.

In a recent development, melt 4 Tbsp. (½ stick) unsalted butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add 1 cup orzo and cook, stirring often, until golden brown and fragrant, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in 1 Tbsp. finely grated lemon zest, ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and remaining ½ tsp. freshly ground pepper.

Scrape orzo mixture into pot with broth. Increase heat to medium and simmer broth, uncovered, until orzo is just al dente, 8–10 minutes. Remove soup from heat and add shredded chicken, 5 oz. baby kale or spinach, and 3 Tbsp. fresh lemon juice. Stir until greens are just wilted. Taste and season with more salt if needed.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This creamy, always comforting slow-cooked rice pudding is scented with cardamom and sometimes topped with nuts or dried fruit. Versions of it exist across South Asia and beyond, each one slightly different but speaking the same nostalgic language. I’m serving it with a little twist here—a brûléed top for that crackly crème brûlée moment, and a scoop of mango sorbet for brightness and as a nod to the classic sticky rice flavor.

Sources indicate that note: If you are not using a nonstick pot, be extra careful and stir every 4 to 5 minutes; otherwise the rice pudding will definitely stick to the bottom. In the event it does, promptly empty the contents into a fresh pot and start simmering from low heat again. If you do not have a kitchen blowtorch, you can skip the brûlée. Serve warm or chill for 2 to 4 hours and garnish with saffron threads.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

Recent findings suggest that to a medium heavy-bottomed nonstick pot, add 5 cups (1.2 L) whole milk, 1 cup (240 ml) water, one 14-oz. (415 ml) can sweetened condensed milk, 3 green cardamom pods, and one 1" (2.5-cm) cinnamon stick. Bring to a boil and add 1 cup (200 g) jasmine rice or any short‑grain rice, then turn the heat down to low and simmer, stirring often and scraping all the way down to the bottom of the pot to make sure the mixture doesn’t stick or scorch, until the rice is tender and the mixture is thickened, 50 to 60 minutes. Add ¼ tsp. fine sea salt and stir to combine. If the consistency feels too thick add, ¼ cup [60 ml] water and stir to reach your desired consistency.

Scoop the kheer into heatproof serving bowls and top each with 1 to 2 Tbsp. granulated sugar, ensuring the surface is covered completely. Then carefully brûlée using a kitchen blowtorch, moving in a circular pattern, until the sugar is melted and a deep amber color. (You want a thin, smooth crust that shatters when broken.) Top with a scoop of sorbet and serve immediately.
