Senate Republicans lament midterms, weigh leadership election delay

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.
  • But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the new Congress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.

But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the new Congress.

The conference was supposed to begin its leadership elections Tuesday morning, but pushed those back to hear from members still reeling from the midterm results, which saw the GOP lose their Senate majority. As the conference meeting turned into what some dubbed an “open-mic session,” they took a break to attend previously scheduled committee hearings, with a plan to return at 2 p.m. Next they must decide whether to forge ahead and pick leaders Tuesday or to punt those choices to a different day.

It has been revealed that sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., stated the conversation taking place was “honest” and “frank.”.

“I will vote for the delay,” he mentioned. “We’ve got a lot of things that we’ve got to think through, and I think to rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

“If you don’t think after losing seven seats minimum that we need to change course, I don’t know what planet you’re on,” he said, adding he was frustrated that his party didn’t do more to focus on topics like affordability ahead of the midterms. “I know it’s easy to blame other people, but we need to look at what has happened here.”.

According to recent reports, sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., who is leading the charge to delay the leadership elections and collected signatures to call the conference meeting beforehand, called it “a very high-quality conversation” in which he was “leading.”.

According to recent reports, preparing for such a big game is no small feat, of course—even if a pro like Jefferson makes it look easy. Ahead of hitting the field, you can often find him getting ready both physically and mentally. “Preparation is everything: I want to make sure I'm confident, focused, and ready to perform at my best,” he says. How did he prepare for Mexico City? “A big part has been making sure I'm physically and mentally ready for the challenges of playing at a higher altitude,” Jefferson says. (Mexico City is about 1.4 miles above sea level—much more intense than even Denver’s Mile High Stadium.) “I've been using the altitude chamber to help my body acclimate. Mentally, it’s about studying the plays, understanding the different schemes, and making sure we're approaching the game with the right mindset.”.

It has been revealed that A more unexpected way Jefferson gets game-day ready, however: With his intentional tunnel-walk outfits. Yesterday, before the athletes even hit the field, Jefferson wanted to rock a meaningful look that would put him in the right mindset for his Mexico City matchup—so he enlisted one of the city’s most well-known designers, Patricio Campillo, to craft a custom look for him. “I've always tried to make my tunnel looks reflect where I am in the world, especially when we're playing internationally,” indicates Jefferson. “For me, fashion is an opportunity to connect with different cultures and showcase designers who bring something unique to the table.”.

A very cool moment for me: Meet the designer—Patricio Campillo—behind the look.

According to recent reports, wanting to rep a design that represented the local culture, Jefferson called up Campillo to start ideating his custom look. He was drawn to the designer for his unique craftsmanship, creativity, and attention to detail. “Choosing Campillo felt like a natural decision—I was genuinely impressed,” says Jefferson. “You can tell how much time, passion, and hard work goes into creating these looks. Being able to represent that craftsmanship on an international stage is something I think is really special.”.

Recent findings suggest that together, they landed on doing a cool, modern take on tailoring. Campillo created a cropped, boxy-style jacket with brown leather trousers—a signature element of the label that the designer wanted to introduce to a whole new audience. “It’s exciting to see someone of Justin’s caliber embrace Campillo,” he says. “I’ve always believed that fashion has the power to bring together people from different backgrounds, so seeing an athlete like Justin connect with our work is especially meaningful.”.

He accessorized with pieces such as a horsehair bag, Oakley shades, and his signature chains. When the wide receiver put on the final look for the first ime, he was immediately drawn to the finer details. “One of my favorite details was the horsehair incorporated into the bag,” claims Jefferson. “It’s such a unique touch and gives the piece a lot of character.” He also appreciated the hand-craftsmanship. “Knowing how much time and effort goes into creating each piece makes you appreciate the look even more,” he says. “I love wearing things that have a story behind them, and this outfit definitely does.”.

The fit, custom made by Patricio Campillo.

In a recent development, it’s not the first time that Jefferson has flexed a fashion statement for his tunnel walk. During past games, he has worn everything from Off-White to Louis Vuitton and Chrome Hearts. What he wears and experiments, of course, depends on the setting. “My tunnel looks are really an extension of my personality, and how I’m feeling that day,” he says. “There are a few things I consider when putting a look together: my mood, who we’re playing, and the brands or designers I want to showcase. Fashion has become another creative outlet for me, and I enjoy stepping outside of what people might expect.”.

Recent findings suggest that this fluid approach to dressing applies to his off-duty wardrobe, too. Jefferson states he enjoys playing around with fashion even on his days off. “Right now, I'd describe my personal style as evolving,” he says. “I'm really focused on experimenting with different looks and exploring styles I might not have considered earlier in my career. I like stepping out of my comfort zone and being open to trying new things. Fashion is all about self-expression, and I think the more willing you are to take risks, the more you learn about yourself and what you like.”.

What does this mean for the rest of Jefferson’s NFL season? You can expect tons more tunnel-walk outfits, for starters. “Every week is another opportunity to bring something exciting to the tunnel,” he claims. “We love finding ways to surprise people, turn heads, and keep things interesting.” Start taking your bets—fashion bets, not sporting bets—on what runway outfit or custom creation he will don next. “We’ve already had a few outfits this season that have gotten a lot of attention, and that’s always fun to see,” he says. “But for me, it’s not just about getting people talking—it’s about continuing to discover upcoming brands, experimenting with different styles, and finding creative ways to express myself through fashion.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every cuisine has a sauce that’s an absolute essential—a ride or die, if you will. For South Asian food, this is a cilantro mint green chutney. It brings a punchy, herb-packed burst of flavor that goes with pretty much everything. This recipe combines cilantro, mint, and just the right amount of heat from green chiles, creating a balance of spice and freshness. Lime juice adds brightness, while cumin, sugar, and chaat masala add complexity. Use this as a zesty topping for your favorite dish or as a base for pani puri water (just add 1½ cups [360 ml] of water and strain), or make it creamy with yogurt or sour cream to use for spreading and dipping.

Slow-roasting Japanese sweet potatoes flesh-side down releases their natural sugars, caramelizing and deepening their sweetness. The flesh becomes incredibly tender, almost custard-like in texture, while the skin turns a rich golden brown and becomes slightly crispy. So don’t bother peeling them! Top them with tamarind concentrate (I like Tamicon, Cock Brand, Pure Indian Foods, or Dragonfly—anything without citric acid), green chutney, fresh onions, tomatoes, and cilantro for a chaat-inspired appetizer.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

According to recent reports, to a blender or food processor, add 2 bunches cilantro (about 6 oz. [170 g]), leaves and stems, 1 bunch mint (about 2 oz. [55 g]), leaves and tender stems, 6 green Thai chiles or 2 serranos, stemmed (more if you want it spicier), ½ cup (120 ml) lime juice (from about 5 limes), 2 tsp. cumin seeds, 1½ tsp. fine sea salt, 1 tsp. sugar, and 1 tsp. chaat masala. Pulse for a few seconds in intervals until the ingredients are pulverized into a smooth paste. Transfer to an airtight container and store until ready to use, up to 1 week in the refrigerator or 1 month in the freezer.

Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Drizzle the sheet with extra-virgin olive oil and place 1½ lb. (680 g) Japanese or Korean sweet potatoes, ends trimmed, halved lengthwise, cut-side down. Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until golden and caramelized on the cut side and cooked through and tender; a knife inserted into the center of the potato should slide through easily. Let rest for 5 to 8 minutes. Once cool enough to handle, cut the sweet potatoes into 1" to 2" [2.5 to 5 cm] pieces.

To a small bowl, add ½ cup (120 g) plain whole-milk yogurt or sour cream and ½ tsp. fine sea salt and whisk to combine. If you’re using sour cream, thin it out with a little water.

Sources indicate that place the sweet potatoes on a serving platter and drizzle the yogurt, ½ cup Evergreen Chutney, 3 Tbsp. tamarind concentrate or paste, and 2 Tbsp. lime juice evenly all over. Sprinkle with 1 medium red tomato (5 oz. [140 g]), finely chopped, 1 small red onion (7 oz. [200 g]), finely chopped, 2 Tbsp. chopped cilantro leaves and tender stems, 1 tsp. chaat masala, 3 green Thai chiles or 1 serrano, stemmed, thinly sliced, and crispy sev and serve immediately.

Do Ahead: You can make the individual components a day ahead of time and store them in airtight containers in the refrigerator, then assemble to serve.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • “The first rule of acting is that you don’t judge your character,” Julia Garner told an enthralled audience on Thursday evening at Manhattan’s Paris Theater, moments after the credits rolled following the world premiere of The Altruists.
  • After a screening of the surprisingly humorous pilot episode, Garner and her co-star, Anthony Boyle, joined the show’s creator, Graham Moore, for a panel discussion with actor-turned-journalist Ben McKenzie about the treachery, trickery, and turbulence that pervade the world of cryptocurrency.
  • According to recent reports, the series doesn’t just chronicle the shocking fall of Bankman-Fried and FTX.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“The first rule of acting is that you don’t judge your character,” Julia Garner told an enthralled audience on Thursday evening at Manhattan’s Paris Theater, moments after the credits rolled following the world premiere of The Altruists. The Netflix original series, available on the streaming platform now, sees Garner step into the shoes of Caroline Ellison, the disgraced co-CEO of Alameda Research and on-again, off-again girlfriend of FTX co-founder Sam Bankman-Fried. “I wasn’t necessarily thinking of the fraud. I just wanted people to be able to understand her,” she added.

After a screening of the surprisingly humorous pilot episode, Garner and her co-star, Anthony Boyle, joined the show’s creator, Graham Moore, for a panel discussion with actor-turned-journalist Ben McKenzie about the treachery, trickery, and turbulence that pervade the world of cryptocurrency. “You’re probably wondering what’s Ryan Atwood doing up here,” McKenzie joked from the stage, referring to his early-aughts turn as one of The O.C.’s leading teen heartthrobs. “For the last four years, I’ve been investigating and documenting fraud and other criminal activity… And having met and interviewed the real Sam Bankman-Fried, I would like to say that Anthony has a lot more charm [than him].”.

According to recent reports, the series doesn’t just chronicle the shocking fall of Bankman-Fried and FTX. Rather, it centers largely on the romantic trajectory of the two financial-industry protégés. “It’s the story of two people who I genuinely, to the core of my being, believe got into this for the right reasons and wanted to do the right thing,” Moore said. “But over the course of their tortuous relationship and those six years, they turned each other into people who did the exact opposite of the thing they initially set out to do.” (Drawing a laugh from the crowd, Northern Irish actor Boyle likened their dynamic to “something from an episode of Love on the Spectrum.”).

After the panel, Garner, in a custom ballet-slipper-pink jumpsuit by Haider Ackermann for Tom Ford and an earful of Lorraine Schwartz bling, and an all-black-clad Boyle joined their castmates, crew members, and press for an after-party in The Plaza Hotel’s Oak Room—making it one of the last industry events to be hosted in the storied venue before it closes for a four-year renovation.

Over mini-umbrella-adorned mai-tais and passed bites, guests discussed the show and compared notes on how much they actually understood crypto terminology, while twirling SBF-approved fidget spinners and branded poker chips around in their hands.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that chair Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., conducts a news conference with members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus during a 2025 retreat in Leesburg, Va.
  • The leaders of an effort to overhaul how the House deals with sexual misconduct hope their proposal will see action before the end of the 119th Congress, though they’re split on the odds.
  • Kat Cammack, R-Fla., chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, remarked legislative text is done and is being looked at by the relevant committees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that chair Teresa Leger Fernández, D-N.M., conducts a news conference with members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus during a 2025 retreat in Leesburg, Va. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

The leaders of an effort to overhaul how the House deals with sexual misconduct hope their proposal will see action before the end of the 119th Congress, though they’re split on the odds.

Rep. Kat Cammack, R-Fla., chair of the Republican Women’s Caucus, remarked legislative text is done and is being looked at by the relevant committees.

Recent findings suggest that “Yes, absolutely,” she said when asked if the package would get a vote this year. “We’re shopping it now with the different committees, House Admin and Ethics, and waiting on their final feedback, which we should have actually this week.”.

It has been revealed that rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, chair of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, remarked she was still optimistic about getting it done, but stopped short of putting full faith in Republican leadership to get it over the finish line. The effort has been underway since May, when Cammack and Leger Fernández’s caucuses unveiled a partnership to propose changes after two members of the House resigned amid allegations of sexual misconduct.

Asked if she thought Speaker Mike Johnson would put the proposal on the floor during the busy lame-duck session, Leger Fernández laughed.

“Hopefully, that’s something that will happen, because you know the Republican Women’s Caucus had mentioned they were optimistic before we left. I’m still optimistic,” she said.

The two groups have spent months holding dozens of meetings with staff, their own caucuses and male members of Congress, among others. Suggestions have included banning members of Congress from engaging in sexual relationships with any House staffer, not just those who work for them directly, and outlining penalties for violaters. Initially, the groups were expected to unveil their work by August recess, but that got pushed back as the House canceled weeks in session and as they cited a desire to get it right.

Cammack stated she thinks Johnson “has been very sincere in his efforts on this.”.

Sources indicate that “That would be a tremendous disappointment” if he didn’t put it on the floor, she stated when asked about the possibility. “I genuinely believe he cares about this problem.”.

Leger Fernández mentioned if it doesn’t get done by the end of the 119th Congress, she hopes some changes would be adopted under the rules package for the next Congress that Democrats bring forward in January. Such packages are typically adopted with party-line votes and give incoming majorities the chance to tweak how the House operates to their liking. While certain narrower proposals aimed at curbing sexual harassment could be written into House rules, others would need to pass both chambers and be enacted into law to take effect.

“We are going to move to make sure it is in the rules package, because we will be in charge next year,” Leger Fernández noted. “But I would love for it to pass now, because that was a commitment that it be bipartisan.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that this recipe is inspired by the garam masala my mother used to make back in India. Just a pinch adds incredible depth and flavor to both meat and vegetable dishes—it’s the secret ingredient that often leaves my guests wondering why my Indian food tastes so exceptional. And now you can use it too! This version perfectly balances the warming notes of cloves and nutmeg, and it’s the one I return to time and time again. If you prefer a sweeter blend, add more cinnamon and fennel seeds; if you want a spicier kick, increase the black pepper and cloves.

Find more Rachel Gurjar recipes here.

1 hour (plus 1 hour for marinating).

In a small bowl, toss 12 dried bay leaves, 12 whole cloves, 5 black cardamom pods, 4 whole star anise pods, three 3" (7.5-cm) cinnamon sticks, 1 whole nutmeg, 3 Tbsp. coriander seeds, 3 Tbsp. whole mace fronds, 2 Tbsp. cumin seeds, 1 Tbsp. black peppercorns, and 2 tsp. white poppy seeds to combine.

Recent findings suggest that heat a medium dry skillet over low heat until hot. Add the spice mixture and toast until slightly fragrant, about 45 seconds. Transfer back to the bowl and let cool.

Recent findings suggest that transfer the whole nutmeg to a mortar and break into smaller pieces with a pestle (this is just to make it easier to grind, so don’t worry about being too precise!). Repeat with the cinnamon. Tear the bay leaves into smaller pieces. Transfer all of the spices to a spice grinder and grind into a fine powder (it will be slightly warm when you remove the lid). Transfer to an airtight container (do not cover yet) and let cool completely. Then close the lid.

In a recent development, do Ahead: Garam masala can be made 1 month ahead. Cover and store in a cool, dark place.

Industry observers note that to a small heatproof bowl, add 1 medium yellow onion (9 oz. [255 g]), halved, thinly sliced into half-moons, 2 Tbsp. lime juice, 2 Tbsp. Kashmiri red chili powder, 2 tsp. chaat masala, ½ tsp. cayenne powder, and ½ tsp. fine sea salt.

In a small pan over medium-high heat, warm 2 Tbsp. peanut oil or any vegetable oil or avocado oil until it shimmers. Add 1 tsp. cumin seeds and cook until fragrant and they start to turn brown, about 1 minute. Be careful not to let the seeds burn or they will taste bitter. Remove from the heat and pour the hot oil over the onions. Toss to coat the onions in the spice mixture.

Serve immediately or let cool and store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

Sources indicate that to a mortar and pestle or food processor, add one 2" (5-cm) piece fresh ginger, chopped, 4 garlic cloves, peeled, and 3 green Thai chiles or 1 serrano, stemmed, chopped, and pound or pulse into a chunky paste. To a medium bowl, add 2 lb. (910 g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs, excess fat trimmed, cut into 2" [5-cm] pieces, along with the ginger-garlic paste and 1 tsp. fine sea salt and toss to combine. Cover and place in the refrigerator to marinate for a minimum of 1 hour or overnight.

Sources indicate that in a medium heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-low heat, warm ⅓ cup (80 ml) vegetable oil or avocado oil, then add 1 tsp. cumin seeds, ½ tsp. black mustard seeds, ½ tsp. black peppercorns, 5 whole cloves, 1 fresh or dried bay leaf, 1 star anise, and one 3" [7.5-cm] cinnamon stick, broken into small pieces, and lightly toast and until fragrant, about 1 minute. Increase the heat to medium, add 1 medium red or yellow onion (9 oz. [255 g]), finely chopped, cover, and cook until the onion is translucent and beginning to turn brown around the edges, stirring halfway through, about 10 minutes.

It has been revealed that add 1 Tbsp. ground coriander, 1 Tbsp. Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 Tbsp. Garam Masala, 2 tsp. cayenne powder, and 1 tsp. powdered turmeric. Stir to combine and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute. Drain off the excess marinade from the chicken, then add it to the pot along with 3 Tbsp. tomato paste, 1 Tbsp. packed fresh fenugreek leaves, and remaining 1½ tsp. fine sea salt and stir until everything is mixed thoroughly and the chicken is covered with the spices and tomato paste. Add ½ cup (120 ml) water and mix again. Cover and cook until the chicken is cooked through and tender, 30 minutes, stirring halfway through.

Remove from the heat and sprinkle with the remaining 1 tsp. Garam Masala, remaining 1 tsp. fresh fenugreek leaves, and cilantro leaves. Serve immediately with lime wedges, Insanely Addictive Pickled Onions, and steamed rice or Indian flatbread.

Do Ahead: Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 1 month.

#180524. Experts on How to Brighten Under Eyes

📅 14 Nov 2025 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1671 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Vogue ↗ Open Full Page

Experts on How to Brighten Under Eyes

📅 14 Nov 2025 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1671 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vogue

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Without fail, the eyes are usually the first place a busy week (or month) highlights up.
  • Recent findings suggest that some of it comes down to how the area is built.
  • There are plenty of ways we can brighten, lift, and hydrate this area of the face.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Without fail, the eyes are usually the first place a busy week (or month) highlights up. A late night, skipping your skin-care routine, or long flight easily translates to a little puffiness in the morning or some shadowing underneath, and maybe even the dreaded “eye bag.” It happens to everyone, and it usually fades once you’ve caught up on sleep, gotten back on your regimen, and have hydrated enough.

Recent findings suggest that some of it comes down to how the area is built. The skin around the eyes is thinner than on the rest of the face, so whatever’s going on underneath, like fluid that settled overnight or tiny blood vessels close to the surface, is easier to see. Over time, collagen gradually decreases and the brows can sit a touch lower, which is a completely normal part of getting older. Still, it’s nice to have a few tricks for the days you want to look as awake as you feel.

The good news? There are plenty of ways we can brighten, lift, and hydrate this area of the face. Some are as easy as curling your lashes or keeping a couple of spoons in the freezer. Other methods, like an eye cream with studied ingredients, work slowly over a few months after a little consistency. If you want to go further, in-office treatments can subtly lift the brow or soften dark circles. Below, our experts share their best tips for brightening and lifting the eye area, starting with the simplest.

Makeup artist Lynsey Alexander has transformed many a tired eye in her time, having worked with models backstage at fashion indicates and on shoots for years. She always begins with good eye drops. “I then use a beige pencil secretly inside the eyes–it needs to be a skin-toned color, white is too stark,” she says. “My favorite is from Paris Berlin as it’s quite dry and not overly creamy, something you don’t want as it moves too easily.”.

“Dark circles are a common complaint in my office,” indicates aesthetic doctor, Maryam Zamani, MD. “One of the most common reasons for dark circles is loss of volume in the periorbital area. As we age, the eyelid-cheek junction becomes elongated, and where this junction was once confluent in youth, it becomes demarcated, giving the appearance of dark lower eyelids or tear troughs.” It’s a common problem that can begin from as early as your twenties, and is made worse as collagen stores deplete. Dr. Zamani often treats it with “meticulously placed micro-droplets of hyaluronic acid” to restore the lost volume and hydrate. You will see brighter, more awake eyes immediately.

Recent findings suggest that celebrity makeup artist Mary Phillips has prepped clients like Hailey Bieber and Kendall Jenner for years, and she knows tired eyes are usually the first thing to give a face away. Her fix starts with a step she has coined called underglazing. “The under-eye area is one of the first places I focus on when prepping the skin because it’s so delicate, and can show dryness and fine lines more easily,” she says. “‘Underglazing’ is really about giving that area the hydration it needs before applying any makeup. I love using lightweight, hydrating skin care and gently pressing it into the skin to help everything absorb. The goal is to make the skin look naturally plump and hydrated, so you need less makeup to begin with.”.

The new wave of the best eye creams are more effective than ever before, and come loaded with efficacious active ingredients to illuminate the area and soften fine lines, while maintaining the integrity of the skin barrier. “Tretinoin has the best evidence behind it–with continued use (for about a year), you see increased cell turnover; cue brightening of the skin and a reduction in wrinkles,” explains dermatologist Emma Craythorne, MD. “Azelaic acid is also brilliant at brightening, if used in strength at five per cent.”.

In a recent development, if your problem is puffiness, take care to ensure you opt for a detoxifying eye cream instead of a hydrating formula–according to Dr. Zamani, hydrating eye creams (particularly those with hyaluronic acid) may exacerbate it.

Yes, it’s boring, but what you eat and drink does make a major difference to the eye area. Those who have ever woken up the morning after with eyes that feel like lead will know that. “Keeping salt and alcohol low in your diet is key,” notes Dr, Zamani. “And sleeping with a pillow and eye mask can also help.”.

To stimulate the area and help de-puff, facialist Nichola Joss recommends gently massaging an eye cream or gel around the outer orbital bone. “You can also use cold teaspoons to gently stimulate, de-puff, improve lymph drainage and brighten the area,” she notes. For those more serious about texture and pigmentation, she also recommends the Lyma Laser, which can be used at home.

Industry observers note that turns out there are a lot of veins and capillaries underneath delicate, thin skin in the eye area, which can cause the dark hue we recognize as dark circles. “We can use sophisticated lasers to target the vascular plexus in the upper and lower eyelid,” notes aesthetic surgeon, Costas Papageorgiou, MD, who works from Harrods Wellness Clinic in London. “This plexus tends to become more prominent with age as a result of accumulative inflammation and loss of elasticity, to name two.” By addressing (and softening) this area, you can reinstate skin clarity and light reflection–plus it works particularly well when combined with under eye filler.

To address cool tones and general darkness in the area, try color correcting. “For blue undertones, opt for a peach-based concealer,” advises Dr. Alexander, who also adds a touch of YSL’s cult Touche Eclat to reflect light in the area. “Then, set the under eyes with a brightening powder, such as Laura Mercier’s Secret Brightening Powder, for added radiance.”.

Simple but effective, curling your eyelashes has an immediate refreshing effect. “Creating a bright, lifted eye is about creating space between the brow and lash line, and drawing attention outwards and upwards,” explains Anna Payne, UK Chanel makeup artist. For a little extra oomph, she suggests applying a dot of highlighting shadow on the centre of the eyelid and inner corner of the eye to create an illuminating spotlight effect.

It has been revealed that when we analyze drooping or lackluster eyes, we don’t often consider that part of the problem might be coming from the forehead. “One of the biggest reasons that the eye area looks tired is that on top of the tiny repetitive blinking movements our eyes have to do each day, we also express an array of emotions through them, too,” says Ada Ooi, TCM practitioner and founder of 001 Skincare. “A lot of our eye movements, such as frowning or surprise, come from muscles in the forehead.” She recommends using a gua sha tool to alleviate the tension built in the frontalis muscles (the vertical muscles that lift the brows). Try cross-friction massage (horizontally, in this case) to break them from their usual position, and release fascia stress.

It has been revealed that “Freshly threaded brows have transformational powers,” sys Vanita Parti MBE, founder of Blink Brow Bar. “By de-fluffing, removing excess stragglers and creating two neat, symmetrical brows, you open up the eyes immediately.” Lifting the arch also lifts and sculpts the entire face, so post-thread, seek to define them with a brow pencil or pomade.

If curling your lashes is already part of your morning, think of this as the version that lasts. Lash lift technician and founder of beauty studio Studio.Lbb recommends it to anyone who’d rather skip the curler altogether. “A lash lift enhances your natural lashes by lifting, curling and tinting them for a longer, darker and more defined look—without extensions or mascara,” she says. Results usually last six to eight weeks, so it’s a smart one to book before a vacation or a stretch of early mornings.

For a quick lift without needles, celebrity facialist and founder of M.A.S.C. Studio Alessandro Cirino points to microcurrent, which sends low-level electrical currents through the skin to wake up the muscles underneath. “Microcurrent can help tone and firm the eye contour, for a fresher-looking result,” he adds. As for a permanent result, Cirino says the research is still limited. Think of it more as a refresh before a significant day unless you keep up with a daily routine.

Sources indicate that most people think of crow’s feet when it comes to injectables around the eyes, but the brow is the less obvious spot for injection. “When strategically placed, neuromodulators can subtly elevate the outer brow by relaxing the muscles responsible for pulling it downward,” indicates Dr. Casey Goodman, medical director of TIEV. “In the right patient, even a slight elevation can make the eyes appear more open, rested, and refreshed.” Dosing matters more here than almost anywhere else on the face. “Overcorrecting can compromise natural expression or even create heaviness where we intended to create lift,” Goodman says. “The goal isn’t to make someone look treated. It’s to make them look like themselves, without the subtle signs of fatigue that may not reflect how they actually feel.”.

When we test and review a product, we take a holistic approach to deliver well-rounded product recommendations. Skyler Gisondo, Such a Nice Young (Leading) Man

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a wet, quasi-Floridian November afternoon in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn; the sidewalks are plastered with layers of translucent brown and gold leaves.
  • Shirt by Banana Republic Vintage Archive.
  • Industry observers note that we quickly unite in a single mission: to locate and purchase one.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Skyler Gisondo is getting soaked.

It’s a wet, quasi-Floridian November afternoon in Carroll Gardens, Brooklyn; the sidewalks are plastered with layers of translucent brown and gold leaves. We’ve just met at a cafe for a bite; our proposal is to walk to Brooklyn Bridge Park. But the second we step outside, we’re pelted with rain. Gisondo is dressed more for a sunny Southern California boardwalk than these soggy Brooklyn streets: white vintage-ish T-shirt (“Norwalk Seaport’s Oyster School”), canvas pants, brown boots, and the usual Rolex Submariner on his wrist. No hat to cover his thick auburn hair, no jacket, and, crucially, no umbrella.

Jacket by Celine. Shirt by Banana Republic Vintage Archive. T-shirt by Paul Smith. Pants by Raimundo Langois. Watch by Cartier.

Industry observers note that we quickly unite in a single mission: to locate and purchase one. “I have a good feeling about Park Natural,” the actor indicates optimistically, gesturing to the health food store across the way. We splash over to check, and an employee redirects us to a CVS down the street, prompting a nine-block journey under my single umbrella. Gisondo is a supportive partner on the scavenger hunt. He is patient as I lead us the wrong way, carefully holding the umbrella over us both while I look at my phone to course-correct, and takes the lead only with my permission. He matches each of my questions with his own, seemingly determined to maintain the cadence of a conversation, rather than that of an interview. As we walk, the rain gets even heavier, saturating the cuffs of our pants. Gisondo draws a few excited looks of recognition from people on the street, before two passersby attempt to recruit him to their church. “Oh, that’s all right—thank you,” he responds politely.

By the time we finally arrive at the CVS, I’m worried the trek was a mistake—not the type of thing you subject a Hollywood actor to, no matter how easygoing they may seem. But when I offer to buy Gisondo a $20 drugstore umbrella and charge it to GQ, his pale-blue eyes light up and a big smile breaks across his freckled face. “Hoo-ley smokes,” he notes, his voice rising in astonishment. “Thank you.”.

In a recent development, “Heck yeah,” he continues as I navigate through self-checkout. “You know what’s funny? The real ‘pinch me’ moments are this stuff.” He explains with complete earnestness how he grew up reading GQ. “Being a boy, being a young man, I was like, ‘I want to look like these guys.’ It’s almost like Stranger Than Fiction, where you hear the narration in your head or something.”.

When we step outside, it’s stopped raining almost entirely. Still, Gisondo thanks me again. “Spanking brand-new umbrella,” he declares with childlike awe, as if he’s holding the key to the city.

This is how Gisondo moves through the world: present, content, unflappable, well-mannered. An all-around good sport. It’s why, in a 4/20-themed Jimmy John’s campaign transparently angling for virality, he seemed not just willing to play ball but really, truly stoked to be eating a Jimmy John’s sandwich. It’s why the persistent memes that imagine Gisondo as a ’90s kid with a peanut allergy who got “hyper as fuck at recess” feel spiritually, if not always factually, accurate. And it’s those same wholesome qualities—and his ability to wield them in increasingly dark scenarios—that have turned the steady, subtle drumbeat of his acting career into an infectious stomp-clap over the course of a year.

In a recent development, in 2026 thus far Gisondo has appeared as a deadbeat but emotionally literate surfer bro boyfriend in the Apple TV series Brothers, made a charming cameo in a Phoebe Bridgers music video as one of its titular adventure-seeking “Lost Boys,” and received a seven-minute standing ovation at the Venice Film Festival for his absorbing role as a sex offender decoy in Primetime. The day before Thanksgiving he’ll complete his sprint with Focker-In-Law, the latest Meet the Parents sequel, in which Gisondo plays Greg Focker’s well-intentioned but avoidant grown-up son. Next up, he’s got two lead roles in projects tentatively slated for next year: a return to the DC universe of James Gunn’s 2025 Superman, as the unwitting ladies’ man and journalist Jimmy Olsen in the true-crime mockumentary The People vs. Gorilla Grodd, and an A24 comedy called Goblin, where he stars opposite a talking puppet, in a film whose script Gisondo calls “probably the most batshit crazy thing I’ve legitimately ever read.”.

Though these projects take place in wildly different worlds, Gisondo’s characters have one thing in common: They’re nice guys in fraught situations. In a cultural moment where dark, morally slippery antiheroes dominate entertainment as well as real life, Gisondo has carved out a lane as a sincere, scrupulous bright spot. “He reminds me of Michael J. Fox in Back to the Future,” says Danny McBride, who cast Gisondo as aspiring stuntman Gideon, the grounded eldest grandchild of the dysfunctional evangelical family empire in The Righteous Gemstones. “There’s something about him that hearkens back to a simpler time and an innocent time, and it makes you root for him.”.

For a guy with an IMDB credit page almost as long as the CVS receipt that came with his umbrella, the blitz of red-carpet events, late-night TV spots, and awards season buzz for his role in Primetime has been especially surreal. “For the first time, at 30, I’m engaging with the part of this job I haven’t before, in a heightened way,” he says.

Now, with his first real shot at an Academy Award nomination, People magazine calling him the “internet’s boyfriend,” and a 2027 stacked with high-profile parts, Gisondo appears poised to prove that, even in the darkest of timelines, nice guys don’t necessarily finish last. And since his role in Primetime, he’s never been more locked in. “It lit a fire under me that I didn’t know I had before,” he says. “I heard actors say stuff like that in the past, ‘I want to do stuff that scares me,’ and I never got it. And now, light bulb. That’s it. That’s when you feel alive. That’s the point.”.

Industry observers note that up until about age 12, Gisondo wanted to be one of three things when he grew up: an actor, a professional hockey player, and/or a professional basketball player. “I was imagining playing both seasons somehow,” he tells me with a grin at Mister Cheeks, the cafe where we first meet. “I held onto that dream for too long.”.

He recalls really “tearing it up” in the 9-to-10-year-old hockey league—until he moved up to the next age bracket, which widened to include older kids, ages 11 to 14. “That’s the first league where full-contact was allowed,” he notes. “I was 11 and the size of an eight-year-old, and there were dudes who were shaving.” This mismatch in size and ability culminated in a wake-up call on ice: “All I remember is getting hit, and then the next thing I’m on my back, opening my eyes with my parents over me. The game had stopped and that was the day that dream died,” he says—before adding, with a laugh: “Thankfully, the acting thing kept working out.”.

Sources indicate that the acting thing included fewer instances where one might be bodychecked by a pubescent teenager, at least in the literal sense. And by that point, Gisondo was already pretty experienced in the craft. Growing up in Palm Beach, Florida, he was “obsessed with movies,” watching West Side Story on repeat until he’d memorized the entire script. Gisondo got it in his head that he could be an actor. His parents, who are process-oriented oceanic engineers, were skeptical. But when a work project brought his family to the Los Angeles area, his mother finally acquiesced and took him to an audition: a hundred-child call for a national Pizza Hut commercial. Gisondo, a precocious blue-eyed cutie pie with bangs and an underbite smile, landed the part. At the time, his dad was convinced his family was the victim of some kind of scam. In actuality, Gisondo had secured his first professional acting gig—and a Screen Actors Guild card—at the tender age of six, a whole 17 years earlier than his character Dan Plum in Primetime. Fans have since dug up and posted evidence of his acting debut, delighting over “TINY GISONDO.”.

Thus began a string of small roles—as “Chris,” “Ryan,” or “Boy #1”—on a handful of family-friendly TV sitcoms. Gisondo’s parents relocated to Southern California and began homeschooling him to support his budding career. As Gisondo tells it, his mother specifically forbade any Disney and Nickelodeon auditions, in order to keep him far away from child stardom. “You get one childhood, so I think she wanted to preserve as normal of a childhood as she could for me,” he states. “And I’m really grateful that she did that.”.

Industry observers note that that freedom to be a kid helped him play one so well that he has since become a folkloric avatar for carefree adolescence—and the subject of one of the modern media landscape’s few truly benevolent memes. Captioning an old photo of Gisondo (from the press cycle for 2015’s Vacation), fans have imagined him enjoying all manner of nostalgic ’90s-kid activities—doing crazy tricks on trampolines, playing with Nerf guns, buying a Guinness Book of World Records at a book fair.

“Some of them I’m like, Oh my God. This is uncanny,” Gisondo notes excitedly. “These people tap into something.” Gisondo and his friends did, in fact, shoot Nerf guns at each other “point-blank” during sleepovers. As a kid he was “ecstatic” to be on a trampoline. And he keeps a copy of The Guinness Book of World Records on his coffee table to this day.

“At a certain point, with the memes,” he notes, “I feel like they transcended and it became about something else, like it’s not about me anymore. It’s become a vessel for something.”.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, these posts have been passed around long enough that even his girlfriend—rumored to be Sterling Point’s Ella Rubin—seems to have internalized them. “There’s one that’s like, I just know his ass has a peanut allergy or something,” he says. “I don’t have a peanut allergy, but I’ve been with my girlfriend three years, okay? We’ll be at dinner. I’ll go to take a bite from her plate and she’ll very seriously go, ‘Oh no, peanuts.’ And then she’ll go, ‘Why do I always think you have a peanut allergy?’ That’s been happening for years.”.

To Rachel Brosnahan, who starred alongside Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen’s Daily Planet colleague Lois Lane in Superman, the memes speak to a larger appetite for Gisondo’s wholesome qualities. “It feels so in line with something that we were pleasantly surprised and excited by when the first Superman movie came out, which is that being earnest and caring a lot and loving really hard can also be cool,” she indicates. “It’s been awesome to watch a world that feels sometimes increasingly cynical and apathetic embrace that. And it’s not surprising to me that Skyler has become the face of that.”.

Even if Gisondo managed to have plenty of good old-fashioned fun as a kid, being homeschooled for nine years left him with a lasting identity as an outsider. He’d show up to camp each summer, trying to figure out what kids who’d spent the year in school together were into. “And I remember that feeling of exclusion,” he states; the older he got, the more apparent it was. “I remember being 15 and getting auditions for high school kids, and they were at a house party. And I was like”—here Gisondo shifts into a blissfully clueless impression of 15-year-old him— “‘I don’t know what the fuck this is about.’”.

Sources indicate that that was around the time Gisondo enrolled in traditional high school, in pursuit of some quintessential experiences. But by then the kind of parts he was booking made even the most prototypical occasions extraordinary. He attended his senior prom—and brought a date he’d secured by filming a prom-posal video on the set of Night at the Museum: The Secret of the Tomb with the help of his costars Ben Stiller and Robin Williams. (Stiller even paid for his limo the night of, as a “wrap gift.”).

Industry observers note that gisondo would chase his dream of a normal life all the way to University of Southern California’s film school, where he pledged a frat for all of three weeks before dropping out. He managed to attend at least one real-life college party before finally accepting his fate as a full-time actor. “It was not my vibe per se,” he says, as we stroll through a dank tree-lined block of brownstones. “It’s like Lord of the Flies.”.

In a recent development, you could argue that only tip-toeing past these young-adult rites of passage has helped Gisondo preserve a certain old-world aura—untouched by keg stands, gravity bongs, or double-digit daily screen time. “Something about Skyler reminds me of actors from the 30s or 40s, who had a real personality and a kind of street smarts about them,” Stiller says via email. “I could see him in a movie playing one of the Dead End Kids in the 30s, like these kind of Fresh York street kids.”.

Recent findings suggest that gisondo did manage to collect enough real-life memories to call upon in future standout supporting roles like the rich-kid hypebeast nerd in Booksmart or Cooper Hoffman’s smarmy child-actor nemesis in Licorice Pizza. He now measures his life milestones by the types of roles he’s being called to audition for. “I remember when I got sent Fockers, I think it was my first time being a fiancé, and I was like, Oh my God, I’m a kid,” he claims. “And then it hit me like, Wait a minute, most of my friends are engaged. I’m not a kid. I’m not a child bride. This is a completely appropriate age to be doing this.”.

Industry observers note that those years as an outsider have made Gisondo especially attuned to social dynamics. He says he senses when someone is quiet in a group, and will be the one to go talk to the person standing alone in the corner of the party. “A lot of my friends and people I respond to are people who are, I don’t know, weirdos in some way, who maybe do have a more difficult time,” he says. ‘It’s funny, there’ll be moments with my girlfriend where I say something. And she’ll be like, ‘Oh, my God, I forget you were homeschooled for nine years.’”.

According to recent reports, but after turning 30 this past July, he says that he feels more self-assured than ever. “I think you spend a lot of your 20s posturing, trying to find your place, find your lane. And I almost feel like I sprung into consciousness two years ago. At 30, I feel very much like myself for the first time. You know what you like, you know who you are. It becomes almost harder to fake it. You become less interested in faking it. I guess I did always feel that, but there’s an immediacy to that feeling now.”.

Sources indicate that that self-assuredness has only grown with time, notes Beanie Feldstein, who worked with Gisondo on Booksmart and then again, seven years later, on Focker-In-Law. “Skyler has always been very pure and truthful and rooted and that has never changed, but of course we are older and have lived more life,” she claims via email. “He feels like a more settled-in version of the same person I’ve always known.”.

That Gisondo has always felt more at home with the out crowd has made him all the more surprised by his current buzzy moment—much of which can be credited to Primetime, and what he calls “the most challenging” role of his life. The propulsive film fictionalizes the lurid early-aughts reality series To Catch a Predator, hosted by former Dateline NBC correspondent Chris Hansen. Gisondo plays one of the decoys Hansen and his team used to lure sex offenders inside a sting house, an impressionable musical theater fan named Dan Plum—a.k.a. “Decoy Dan”—who’s so eager to kickstart his acting career that he’s initially oblivious to the toxic workplace and mission he’s joined.

In a recent development, unlike Plum, of course, Gisondo was already a known quantity when he auditioned for Primetime, but he desperately wanted the part. As he tells it, Lance Oppenheim offered it to him within the first 10 minutes of their introductory call. “I was used to singing for my supper,” he claims. “But he was so certain. And I remember asking him, ‘What have you seen of mine that makes you so certain?’ Oppenheim, who says he “bookmarked” Gisondo when he saw Licorice Pizza, was drawn to what he describes as “this particular combination of sweetness, humor, and slightly awkward, boyish earnestness.” The director also liked that Gisondo had experience as a child actor, but from the perspective of an older, wiser adult. “I was drawn to the idea that Skyler had spent so much of his life navigating the strange machinery of the entertainment industry himself, and what he might bring to a character who was also trying to find his place within that world,” he told me via email.

After he signed on to the film, Gisondo recalls trying to explain the part to his father, the oceanic engineer. “It was the most exciting opportunity of my career by far,” he says. “I remember telling my dad all of these things: So, it’s an A24 movie, starring Robert Pattinson, this guy Lance Oppenheim. And I would play a guy who’s an aspiring actor who’s used as bait to catch pedophiles in the decoy operations. And I’ll never forget, my dad was kind of quiet and he goes, ‘So this is something you’d be excited about?’”.

According to recent reports, as Dan, Gisondo parades through rented homes in puka shells and tie-dye T-shirts, directing unknowing predators toward a variety of snack foods with a high-pitched, exuberant naivete that manages to both brighten the film’s depraved subject matter and make it feel that much more sinister. (These scenes, too, were GIF’d and memed by the Gisondo hive.) But as we watch Hansen (Robert Pattinson) and his producer Andie Bender (Merritt Wever) plunge deeper into a shameless pursuit of higher ratings, Dan recoils, gradually becoming the closest thing this story has to an ethical center.

In a recent development, “He plays it absolutely honestly, absolutely straight-faced with absolute sincerity,” says Wever, who calls Gisondo’s performance “perfect and undeniable.” “So when there’s comedy to be had—even if it’s uncomfortable or squirmy comedy or cringey comedy or comedy that is uncomfortable because you’re laughing because you can see the heartbreak inside somebody, the true ouch of the vulnerability and the unknowingness—it’s there because he’s not winking at the audience. He’s really inside that part. It has so many colors because he’s playing it so truthfully. That’s a sign of a very smart actor.”.

Recent findings suggest that I point out to Gisondo that this isn’t the first time he’s played a character who becomes the sneaky moral compass of the story. He had something similar going as Gideon in The Righteous Gemstones, where he served as a relief to the over-the-top antics of a completely insane evangelical empire. Considered alongside all those memes about his imagined childhood, a single through-line becomes obvious—in the parts he plays, but maybe also on a human level, he seems to remind people that good still exists in the world.

Recent findings suggest that “What’s funny is hearing you say that—it’s my first time bumping up against perception, in a way. Being perceived on that scale,” he indicates, slowing down to sort through his words for the first time in our otherwise free-flowing conversation, his eyes widening a little. “I think all any of us want is to be seen. I think to be loved is to be seen, in a way. People thinking that about me is the most gratifying possible thing. To me, it communicates I’m doing something right in my life.”.

But even as he’s astonished by the public feedback loop about his persona, he also can’t help but feel a little unnerved by it. “Usually, I feel like, only at your funeral, are you meant to see so many people talking about what they think of you.”.

By this point Gisondo and I have made our way down through Brooklyn Bridge Park, looking out at the Manhattan skyline from a waterlogged pier and then wandering along a few wooded paths to arrive on the edge of Dumbo, where we’re idling as our conversation winds down. Behind him, the Brooklyn Bridge is enveloped in rain clouds. I remind him that people are saying good things.

Recent findings suggest that “Everybody wants to read nice things about them, whether it’s a review, whether it’s a meme,” he says. “There’s no doubt it feels good. I’m not sure I want to feed the part of me that likes how good that feels. That’s the gremlin in all of us.”.

Industry observers note that with that, we say our goodbyes and I turn to make my way to the subway. “Thanks for my umbrella,” he notes. I have no question he really, truly, earnestly means it. ✦.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There’s a time and place for classic cheesecake, but it’s hard to resist a handheld dessert. These irresistible cheesecake bars are the solution. They’re like traditional cheesecake’s cool older sister, and she’s invited to your holiday party this year. These bars perfectly balance creamy, rich cheesecake with the tartness of fresh cranberries and the nuttiness and warmth of a pecan streusel topping, with none of the intensive labor required for traditional cheesecake.

The bars:In this recipe, the cheesecake filling rests in a simple graham cracker crust, and swirls of homemade cranberry sauce weave their way through each bar, adding a burst of flavor and a beautiful marbled effect that makes them almost too pretty to eat—almost. Fresh orange juice and zest bring the cranberry sauce to life and add another layer of brightness and complexity to the bars. The streusel topping, made from a mix of pecans, brown sugar, and cinnamon, adds a satisfying crunch that contrasts beautifully with the creamy cheesecake filling.

The cranberry sauce:If you like, you can simplify this recipe further by using 1 (14-oz.) can of whole berry cranberry sauce rather than making homemade cranberry compote.Storage:Whether you’re making them for a holiday gathering, a potluck, or just because you deserve a delicious treat, these cozy bars are sure to impress. If you’re lucky enough to have any left over, they’ll be amazing with your coffee in the morning; store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for a few days.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A big, billowing cloud of meringue tops this crimson beauty and acts as a sweet reprieve from the tart cranberry curd. The vibrant filling is made even more sour with a generous amount of lime juice. Think lemon meringue pie but holiday-ified. Use our Perfect Pie Crust as the base to create a sturdy-flaky foundation, and be sure to start the pie the day before you plan to serve it, as the curd requires several hours of chilling to set into a sliceable texture. Cut into it too soon and it will run onto your plate, creating a messy—albeit delicious—slice.

In a recent development, we never make pie dough without a metal bench scraper. Our favorite is from Gestura. Use the scraper to cut butter, fold dough and nudge it into shape, transfer it from counter to plastic wrap, trim edges, cut strips, and, sure, scrape flour off your counter.

Welcome to Bon Appétit Bake Club, a community of curious bakers. Each month senior Test Kitchen editors Jesse Szewczyk and Shilpa Uskokovic share a must-make recipe and dive deep on why it works. Come bake and learn with us—ask questions, share pics, listen to our podcast, and lots more here. And don't forget to join the Bake Club Group chat over on Substack.

3 hours (plus 30 minutes for freezing and 5 hours for chilling).

Whisk 1⅔ cups (208 g) all-purpose flour, 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and ¼ tsp. baking powder in a large bowl to combine. Add 2 oz. chilled cream cheese, cut into 1" pieces, and rub into dry ingredients with your fingers until incorporated (mixture will look very shaggy). Add 10 Tbsp. chilled unsalted butter, sliced ½" thick, and toss to coat in flour, then smash with your fingers into smaller, flatter pieces (about chickpea-size).

In a recent development, make a well in the center of mixture and pour in ¼ cup ice water. Toss with a fork or your hands to distribute, then knead in bowl a couple of times to bring dough together (some dry bits may remain).

According to recent reports, turn out dough onto a surface lightly dusted with rice flour or all-purpose flour and dust top of dough with flour. Roll out to a ½"-thick rectangle. Fold dough in half, rotate 90°, and fold in half again. Roll out again to a ½"-thick rectangle and repeat folding process, dusting with more rice flour as needed to prevent sticking. Pat into a ½"-thick disk and wrap tightly in plastic. Chill at least 2 hours and, preferably, up to 12 hours.

In a recent development, let dough disk sit at room temperature 5 minutes. Roll out dough on a lightly floured surface to a 12" round, about ¼" thick. Brush excess flour from dough and wrap around rolling pin. Transfer to a 9"-diameter pie pan (such as East Fork Spun Iron Pie Dish). Unfurl into pan, then lift edges and allow dough to slump down into pan. Trim, leaving about a 1½" overhang. Fold overhang under so crust is flush with edges of pan and crimp as desired with lightly floured fingers. Set pan on a rimmed baking sheet and prick bottom and sides of crust with a fork in several places. Freeze, uncovered, at least 30 minutes and up to 2 hours.

Place a rack in lower third of oven; preheat to 400°. Line crust with a sheet of parchment paper and fill with pie weights or dried beans. Bake crust, tenting edges with foil if browning too quickly, until edges are set and look dry, 20–25 minutes. Carefully lift out parchment paper and weights and continue baking crust, gently pressing bottom and sides occasionally with a flat-bottomed measuring cup if puffing up, until bottom looks dry and is golden, 20–25 minutes more. Transfer pan to a wire rack and let crust cool.

Do Ahead: Dough can be made 1 month ahead. Wrap disk in 2 layers of plastic and freeze instead of chilling. Thaw in refrigerator 12 hours before using.

Bring 1 lb. fresh or frozen cranberries, 1½ cups (300 g) granulated sugar, and ¼ cup water to a boil in a large saucepan, then reduce heat to medium and simmer, stirring often, until cranberries soften and burst and most of the liquid has evaporated, 10–15 minutes. Let cranberry mixture cool.

Transfer cranberry mixture to a blender; reserve pan. Add ⅔ cup fresh lime juice and ¼ cup (32 g) cornstarch and blend on high speed until smooth. Scrape purée back into pan (not over heat) and add 3 large eggs, 2 large egg yolks, 1 Tbsp. vanilla extract, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt. Place over medium heat and cook, whisking constantly, until mixture bubbles and thickens to a pudding-like consistency, about 4 minutes. Remove pan from heat. Add ¾ cup (1½ sticks) unsalted butter, room temperature, cut into pieces, and whisk until melted and combined. Strain curd through a fine-mesh sieve, pushing with a rubber spatula, directly into crust. Smooth into an even layer and cover with plastic wrap, pressing directly onto surface. Chill pie at least 4 hours and up to 1 day.

Sources indicate that just before serving, beat 6 large egg whites, room temperature, ¼ tsp. cream of tartar, remaining 1¼ cups (250 g) granulated sugar, and remaining ½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or ¼ tsp. Morton kosher salt in the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the whisk attachment on medium speed until foamy and sugar is dissolved, about 5 minutes. Increase speed to high and continue to beat until stiff peaks form, about 3 minutes more.

According to recent reports, spoon meringue over filling and swirl decoratively as desired. Using a kitchen torch, toast meringue if desired.

What Is GTA VI Trying to Say About the Manosphere?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, what's a man allowed to like these days?
  • We asked a physical therapist, developers, and other gaming obsessives for the best tips to help you highjack garbage trucks in Leonida for as long as humanly possible.
  • Grand Theft Auto VI, these men assert, is emasculating because it asks players to role-play a man that respects his partner and do mundane tasks she would appreciate, like repaint their bedroom or get her a nice necklace.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, what's a man allowed to like these days? Not the Super Bowl, or Christopher Nolan movies, it seems, each of them guilty of sins against masculinity. Now there is a new offender: Grand Theft Auto VI. Over one brief weekend, Rockstar's long-in the works, exorbitantly expensive opus has given us a rare monocultural moment, and elicited a wounded reaction from a slice of gamers steeped in the streams and podcasts of right-wing figures like Steven Crowder, Zack “Asmongold” Hoyt, and Braden Eric “Clavicular” Peters.

We asked a physical therapist, developers, and other gaming obsessives for the best tips to help you highjack garbage trucks in Leonida for as long as humanly possible.

Grand Theft Auto VI, these men assert, is emasculating because it asks players to role-play a man that respects his partner and do mundane tasks she would appreciate, like repaint their bedroom or get her a nice necklace. For others, it is less that the game is offensively woke, but that its wokeness is getting in the way of their fun. “You can't kiss anyone other than your strong female Latina partner,” complains Crowder, his co-hosts all lamenting that video games ought to be a vehicle for their every base fantasy. These men object to what they see as politics encroaching on what they think ought to be a politics-free space, “shut up and dribble” but for violent video games. But there's a delicious irony to this because the game genuinely has a bone to pick with these unfortunate figureheads of the manosphere.

The manosphere, it should be noted, is a (shitty) state of mind. Less a formal designation than a collection of people who promote similar sexist, racist, and/or fascist ideals, a loose web of podcasters, streamers, and influencers who all preach a gospel of grievance in which men are victims of women withholding sex, liberals withholding power, and other men for not performing masculinity correctly. They can run the gamut from disgraced influencer Andrew Tate (presently in jail awaiting trial for a litany of alleged crimes) to the comedians and podcasters orbiting Joe Rogan's massive audience. But they all have one thing in common: these men and the people who pay rapt attention to them are the targets of Grand Theft Auto VI's satire.

Recent findings suggest that some background here: While yes, Grand Theft Auto VI casts players as modern Bonnie-and-Clyde Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, their story is only one reason to play the game. Another is the incredibly dense setting of Leonida, a feverish and astonishingly lifelike take on Florida, chock full of weirdos and wildlife to take in. Layered on top of that is a whole media ecosystem: a fake Instagram to scroll named Snapmatic, a news feed app, a suite of radio stations with robust programming including two talk radio stations, three TV networks with entire shows, and magazines and books you can read in excerpts.

It has been revealed that it's in all this background material that Grand Theft Auto VI really tears into the modern grievance grift of the manosphere. The game's decade-plus gestation means it's had a lot of time to amass a shooting gallery of noxious conservative male influencers that the algorithm has elevated and buried, ranging from flat-earth conspiracy theorists to MAHA-adjacent cronies. On the Weazel TV network, you can find these views as the punchline of entire Adult Swim-esque cartoons like Right Wing, about a patriotic superhero horrified to learn that a straight pride parade has been transformed by a gay superhero called The Flamer. “All these years suppressing who I was, but now I'm free!” shouts Right Wing's colleague Great Uncle Sam after the Flamer has liberated him. “Isn't that what America is all about?” “No,” Right Wing retorts. “America is about guns, and lots of them!”.

Scroll through Snapmatic, and you can find a clear analogue of Liver King—the content creator who promoted an “ancestral lifestyle” that involved consuming raw animal organs—posting under @paleoprimal. In one of his faux influencer videos, he advises his followers to “start beating your meat,” before dropkicking a hunk of raw flesh. “I don't eat anything unless I've conquered it first.” Ashes of Glory, a sendup of historical war fiction that sits by Jason's bed, is drowning in overly reverent prose that also happens to note that its war heroes are psychopaths. One passage: “'You've been charged with murdering civilians, violating every law known to God and man, calling your enemies rude names and uncontrollable teabagging', said the General. 'Which is exactly why we need your help.'”.

In a recent development, A lot of these blows are glancing, more about attacking attitudes than people, give or take a Liver King. But turn the in-game radio dial to WKTT, Grand Theft Auto VI's conservative talk radio station, and the targets sharpen. Hosts Richard Bastion (Jason Sudeikis) and Dominic "The Brick" Brizzolato (Stavros Halkias) do pastiches of Alex Jones and Nic Fuentes, spouting racist and sexist takes. Ponytails are "the hairstyle of someone who’s about to suck your dick," per Brizzolato, who also maintains local football team the Manatees have problems to do with "culture" and "not race." Every so often they are undercut by callers who ask how performance-enhancing drugs and hair implants don't count as gender-affirming care. Of the many items they hawk—Flaming O's snacks, Sprunk soda, and Patriot beer—the most absurd and on-the-nose is a special playing card set with “no queens.”.

According to recent reports, in its blunt recreation of the conservative male media ecosystem, Grand Theft Auto VI plainly states what Rockstar thinks of these guys: They're really fucking stupid. They are stupid in ways that are true-to-life and moronic in ways that Rockstar exaggerates, but only just so. They drive home this point by underlining the pathetic loneliness subtextual in all these real-life broadcasts, with Richard Bastion asserting that he doesn't have friends but is building "a fraternity with a mission to save America" and that friends "let you down" and "tell the papers that your wife sleeps in a separate bed and sometimes house.".

Recent findings suggest that after 13 years, and a budget rumored to rival that of Dubai’s Burj Khalifa skyscraper, the new Grand Theft Auto is finally here. Our critic's verdict? It's a tour de force that reimagines what a video game can be.

According to recent reports, the message hits cleaner than past iterations of the game not because Grand Theft Auto VI is any less lowbrow than before—it is still awash in dick jokes, memes about shitting your pants, and South Park-esque lambasting of White America—but because this more richly detailed, lifelike version of Grand Theft Auto means the cartoonish aspects stand out all the more. What's a joke and what is not is clearer than it has ever been.

According to recent reports, despite the protests from fans who say the latest iteration of the Grand Theft Auto betrays the spirit of the franchise, there was always evidence that the game hated these hypermasculinity-obsessed tryhards, even before they had a manosphere to inhabit. While early games in the series did not have much in the way of plot or characters, they were tongue-in-cheek caricatures of gangster epics and the ambitions of men within them, a touch of arch Scottish humor (Rockstar's lead Grand Theft Auto team is based in Edinburgh) keeping them from being sincere homages.

Industry observers note that nearly 20 years ago in Grand Theft Auto IV—a series turning point, where the games started to have stories with intentional thematic interests—Rockstar Games incessantly lambasted the pursuit of the hypermasculine. Its protagonist Niko Bellic served as a stoic counterpoint to many of the jacked-up weirdos of the faux-Upcoming York dubbed Liberty City, arriving in the United States during the game's opening credits with nothing but the clothes on his back and his cousin Roman's lies about his own success in his ear. Through Niko's journey, Grand Theft Auto IV posed the argument that this country's obsession with the unfettered pursuit of power and wealth makes people unwell, and that culture afflicts men in ways that render them uniquely delusional. It gives his cousin Roman a fantasy of a success that will never come, causing him to submit to the intimidations of two-bit enforcers. It makes men like Brucie Kibbutz, a supplement-obsessed fitness freak, deny his own obvious interest in men in favor of a nonstop stream of homophobic jokes and crude sexual banter. It makes Niko, a soldier who thought he was escaping his criminal past, find himself immediately becoming a different kind of criminal at the behest of men who believe the world is theirs to take. And that's just in the first few hours.

Industry observers note that grand Theft Auto IV’s skewering came at the expense of others—namely the women and queer people who are the butt of nearly every joke in the game. Seven years later, Grand Theft Auto V would course-correct by being hateful to everyone in its fictional version of Los Angeles: the acai-and-granola liberals and the asshole conservatives alike. It mires itself in the desperation of male entitlement, as three characters—the middle-aged Michael De Santa, the young striver Franklin Clinton, and Trevor Lawrence, the lewd loose cannon—adjust poorly to a world they cannot dominate. De Santa, arguably the protagonist of the three characters the player can inhabit, sees the world as out to emasculate him, either through his wife's affair, his deadbeat son, or his daughter who he must rescue from TV producers that he assumes are predatory. Michael's world is much simpler when he's holding a gun, and Grand Theft Auto V is eager to get one in his hands. In this, it feels like the game wants you to agree: Isn't this more fun than dealing with all that? And it is, because Rockstar made it that way.

Yes, there are missions. But have you seen the kicks?

It has been revealed that there's always been a have-it-both-ways nature to Grand Theft Auto's satire. Rockstar is happy to facilitate the same American male id it's lampooning, and the staggering number of copies sold suggest that even conservative commentators out there appealing to incel logic are logging right onto their PlayStations the moment they stop posting. But despite what critics may claim to their audiences, Grand Theft Auto VI's manosphere parodies are not a huge departure for the series, because the problems with toxic masculinity remain woefully consistent, as do the grifters who seek to profit from it. Insecurity is both a big business and a renewable energy source.

It has been revealed that what's left out of all these complaints about Grand Theft Auto VI being a game where you embody a simp man is that you do not have to do any of the loving behavior these clowns rail against in the video game. You can ignore Lucia when playing as Jason, let your relationship grow distant and decay. You can leave the walls unpainted, never pick up flowers or groceries, not press the button to hold Lucia's hand, keep your distance on the dance floor. The game just makes clear what the real world does not: That's a good way to end up alone. And that’s the one thing the parodied blowhards of GTA VI's in-game manosphere broadcast loud and clear: that they're alone.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this autumn, artists, institutional leaders, collectors, and curators descended on Accra to celebrate a decade of Gallery 1957 and attend Accra Cultural Week, both founded by entrepreneur and art collector Marwan Zakhem.

According to recent reports, since opening in 2016, Gallery 1957 has contributed to the Ghanaian capital’s burgeoning cultural infrastructure. Local artists, Zakhem recalls, “seemed to be doing residencies everywhere” yet they “struggled to make their work here.” So he launched Cultural Week, keen to develop a homegrown creative community while also engaging an international audience. “Cultural Week began because I wanted to bring people to Accra to see what I was seeing.”.

Sources indicate that I arrived for the week-long convening at 7 a.m., fresh from the 10-hour flight from Fresh York. As the early morning traffic recalibrated my senses, sights and sounds reminded me of my first visit there three years ago, when I reported on the opening of Amoako Boafo’s residency dot.ateliers.

Accra Cultural Week includes studio visits, exhibition tours, talks, visits to cultural institutions, and social events. Artist-led spaces and an eclectic nightlife scene underscore how artistic production is shaped just as much by formal institutions as by the social and material conditions of the city’s close-knit communities.

The week began with a performance at the studio of Serge Attukwei Clottey, the multidisciplinary artist who presented the gallery’s inaugural exhibition in 2016. Elsewhere, a tour of Boafo’s studio offered glimpses of work in progress. Just across the street, lunch at Backyard Community Club—a feast of fish stew, spicy jollof rice, and fried sweet plantains with chilled palm wine and sobolo, a local drink made of dried hibiscus, from Palm Moments—offered respite from the midday heat.

Sources indicate that “The biggest thing that stands out to me is the sense of community and generosity here—not just from the gallery, but also the willingness of other artists and institutions to participate,” Nigerian artist Modupeola Fadugba states of Ghana’s art scene. “There is a leadership of community, which has led to more people following that leadership and being communal.” The story of Gallery 1957 is also the story of artists who have built their own institutions. Stops during Cultural Week included Kwesi Botchway’s WorldFaze Art Practice residency; El Anatsui’s studio, which employs dozens of people; and Rita Mawuena Benissan’s Si Hene Foundation.

Recent findings suggest that installation view: “Alvaro Barrington: “Western Beef ft. Western Union,” Limbo Museum, Accra.

Sources indicate that the week continued with a stop at the Nubuke Foundation, now in its 20th year, and a visit to Alvaro Barrington’s exhibition “Western Beef ft. Western Union” at Limbo Museum, housed in an unfinished building on the University of Ghana campus. “The work we’re doing allows us to be radical, experimental, and to have the autonomy to define ourselves,” states the museum’s founder, Dominique Petit-Frère. “As an institution, we can offer artists opportunities to think beyond their practice.” Barrington, in turn, calls the show an “opportunity to present an artwork in Accra at a time when not only Ghana but the globe needs to reimagine how we grow.”.

According to recent reports, launched in 2021, the Yaa Asantewaa Art Prize—named after the Asante queen mother who led a resistance against British forces—provides support to African female artists. For the first time, it extends beyond Ghana to Senegalese women artists, offering a three-month residency exchange between Accra and Senegal, highlighting the gallery’s evolving ambitions.

“Where the Earth Remembers,” Gallery 1957’s 10th-anniversary exhibition, brings together a group of artists that “reflects the breadth and evolving scope” of the gallery’s program, featuring the work of Godfried Donkor, Serge Attukwei Clottey, Tunji Adeniyi-Jones, Rita Mawuena Benissan, Amoako Boafo, and Ibrahim Mahama, who has his own cultural centers, Savannah Centre for Contemporary Art (SCCA) and Red Clay Studio, both in Tamale, in Ghana’s Northern Region.

At Red Clay, Ground Conditions: Tamale—a gathering presented by Limbo Museum and Studio Marant and supported by the Loewe Foundation—featured a conversation between Mahama and the Nigerian designer Nifemi Marcus-Bello. “There is something incredibly inspiring about witnessing his vision extend beyond his individual practice, into the creation of spaces that encourage dialogue, experimentation, and collective thinking,” Marcus-Bello indicates of Mahama.

It has been revealed that as the week ended, I reflected on the collaborations the gallery has forged, moving beyond mere visibility and toward engagement with the ideas and people that sustain the city’s cultural life. For Gallery 1957, the anniversary isn’t just a milestone—it’s also a testament to the artists and institutions that have taken root in its wake.
